gaps.title: New upstream workflows run before Actions hygiene and can read the repository's EW_ secrets
gaps.evidence: APW-02 FR-28 (spec line 298) runs hygiene only AFTER a sync that changed the tracked branch. S18 (lines 191-194) disables a new workflow only 'once the sync pull request is merged'. S4/FR-35 fast-forwards the tracked branch directly, which fires `push` events. The sync PR comes from a branch in the same repository, so workflows it adds run on `pull_request` with repository secrets. CONTRACTS §9 line 436 stores build values as repository-level Actions secrets (`EW_`), which any workflow can read. FR-27 also keeps inherited workflows the member turned back on. The result: a workflow added upstream runs with the user's build secrets before hygiene ever sees it.
gaps.proposedFix: Before a fast-forward, or before creating or updating the sync PR, diff the upstream range for `.github/workflows/**`. When workflows changed, never fast-forward and say so on the card. Make APW-05 scope EW_ secrets to an environment or branch policy that only ever-works-build.yml on the tracked branch can read, so inherited or new workflows cannot reference them. Add an ACC: an upstream commit adding an on:push workflow that echoes secrets is synced and the canary sees nothing.

But the worker calls AgentRunService.execute (packages/tasks/src/tasks/trigger/agent-task-execute.task.ts:314, 605-623). AgentRunContext (packages/agent/src/agents/agent-run.service.ts:74-142) has no runtimeEnvironment or attachedRepos field, and the run is an in-process tool loop over AiFacadeService.createChatCompletion (apps/api/src/agents/agents.module.ts:498-590; agent-run.service.ts:656). runtimeEnvironment is only threaded through FullPipelineExecutorService / PipelineFacadeService (git grep), and nothing on the platform ever passes attachedRepos. claude-managed-agent is a Work-generation pipeline: execute(work, GenerationRequest, existing, options), fixed buildSystemPrompt(), seed manifest, perSessionBudgetUsd read from plugin config (claude-managed-agent.plugin.ts:440-640). Drop the in-sandbox platform tools: questions come through the provision-output 'question' outcome and validation runs in the job. Alternatively, record an owner decision on a different isolated runtime. Update T1, T3, T14, T15, the Skill draft (allowedTools), and CONTRACTS §3 if a new capability method is needed.

gaps.evidence: The workflow is only generated from the applied (effective) App spec: plan.md:963-966 (§7.2 step 1) and plan.md:1010-1013 (listener fires only on app.spec.applied or app.env.changed). APW-04 plan.md:158-161 verifies the proposal's PR head before merge ('open PR … validate … startBuild(head, verification)'), and that PR adds only the App spec and maybe a Dockerfile (README D5). So no ever-works-build.yml exists on the default branch or in the PR. workflow_dispatch needs the workflow file on the default branch, and the pull_request trigger (S6, spec.md:108-110) needs it in the PR. The normative sketch also skips building: the build, secret-check and Push steps carry `if: inputs.ew_mode != 'verify'` (plan.md:189, 213, 217). gaps.title: Pull-request and verification builds hand every EW_ build secret to code no human has reviewed
gaps.evidence: In the APW-05 plan §2 workflow, the build job's `if` (line 166) admits pull requests from the same repository, and build-args pass `<NAME>=${{ secrets.EW_<NAME> }}` (line 202). Agents open their pull requests from branches in that same repository: App Provisioner proposals, evolve-loop Task branches (APW-08) and the `ever-works/upstream-sync` branch (APW-02). Those branches build the PR head's Dockerfile and package scripts on GitHub-hosted runners, which have open egress. FR-21 (spec line 255) scans only the image metadata. FR-53 also sends owner-set prompted values to the agent-written proposal through `EW_VERIFY__PROMPTED`. The APW-08 FR-20 guard protects `.github/workflows/**` but not Dockerfiles or `package.json`. ACC-NEG-05 plants the honeytoken "under a name no fixture code reads" (ACCEPTANCE.md line 366), so it passes even though nothing blocks the leak.
gaps.proposedFix: APW-05: pull-request and verification builds get no secret build value. Use throwaway generated values; these builds are already not deployable. Alternatively, move EW_ values into a GitHub Environment limited to the tracked branch and the ever-works-build workflow. Deliver prompted values to a verification only after the owner approves the diff of the build files (Dockerfile, lockfiles, package scripts). Add an ACC: the honeytoken is a `fromEnv` build value that the injection fixture's Dockerfile reads on an agent PR, and the canary sink receives nothing. Update ACC-NEG-05.

gaps.title: Push and pull-request Builds are discovered only from webhook deliveries, and no epic installs a webhook on the data repository
gaps.evidence: APW-05 plan §7.5 (L998-1004): only `AppBuildWorkflowRunConsumer` creates Build rows for push and pull_request runs. The sweep (§7.4 L991-996) only re-polls existing `queued`/`running` rows. The plan admits 'No webhook is guaranteed … App deliveries may not cover a fork' (L80). EXISTING-SUBSTRATE L70: 'nothing installs a webhook on a user repository'. APW-02 FR-55 (spec L360) adds only the `createWebhook?` capability, and no task in APW-02 or APW-05 calls it. APW-05 spec FR-34 (L290) still promises discovery 'by event or by polling'. Without a delivery, the first Build (workflow commit), every post-merge Build (ACC-E2E-07/14) and sync-merge Builds are never recorded. Consequently `app.build.succeeded` never fires, auto-deploy never starts and APW-08 delivery stays at `merged` (APW-08 plan L230-233 only reads WorkBuild rows).
gaps.proposedFix: Pick one or both. (1) APW-05 `app-build-prepare` installs the signed repository webhook (events workflow_run, push, pull_request) through APW-02 `createWebhook` after writing the workflow, and removes it on App Work deletion. (2) Add a discovery pass to `app-build-sweep`: for each App Work whose tracked-branch head (or open same-repo PR head) has no Build row, call `listWorkflowRuns(file, head_sha)` and upsert. gaps.title: The Trigger worker cannot host app-deploy as planned: in-process services, event relay to Activity, dispatcher wiring and the no-runtime fallback are all undefined
gaps.evidence: T32 (tasks.md:441-451) creates four Trigger tasks but never names the Nest module they boot. At HEAD, worker services reach the API through remote proxies (packages/tasks/src/trigger/worker/modules/trigger-internal.module.ts:51-60 onward, served by apps/api/src/trigger/trigger-internal.controller.ts:163-201,456). If `app-deploy` follows that pattern, the cluster is dialled from the API, which breaks FR-5. If it does not, nothing says which repositories, AppSpec/license/env sources or NotificationService run in the worker. T28 maps Activity with `@OnEvent` in apps/api/src/activity-log/activity-log.listener.ts, but events emitted with EventEmitter2 inside the worker never reach that API-process listener. plan.md:667 says the facade throws when *constructed* outside the worker, yet T20 (tasks.md:295-302) registers it in `FacadesModule`, which the API boots. (b) The arity pin at `packages/agent/src/tasks/__tests__/job-runtime.providers.spec.ts:134-143`. (c) What happens when the registry returns `null` (job-runtime.providers.ts:160-176: the call site's in-process dev fallback), which would run cluster I/O in the API and leaves the PR — cluster lane with no runtime.

(5) The null-runtime behaviour: refuse with `worker_not_isolated` in production; outside production use an explicit local worker mode for the PR — cluster lane. gaps.title: Circular ordering: in-cluster dependencies need namespace policies that only a Deployment creates, while a Deployment needs dependencies Ready
gaps.evidence: APW-07 plan §4.9 (L533-535): k8s providers 'verify both [`ew-default-deny` + `ew-allow-deps`] exist before provisioning and otherwise fail `namespacePoliciesMissing`'; objects live 'in the App Work's namespace chosen by APW-06'. APW-06 creates the Namespace and NetworkPolicies only in Deployment phase 1 `prepare` (plan §4.2 L313; spec FR-26 row 1), and FR-10 names the namespace 'at first Deployment'. APW-06 FR-24 (spec L325-329) refuses to start a Deployment until 'every dependency is ready'. No `app-cluster-op` creates the namespace beforehand (plan §9.2). The two policies also disagree in meaning: APW-06 `ew-allow-deps` covers egress to dependencies outside the namespace (plan L434). Every App Work with postgres on Your cluster (fixture, Umami, Cal.diy) can never reach a first Deployment.
gaps.proposedFix: Add an APW-06 `app-cluster-op` op `prepare-namespace` (namespace, labels, `ew-default-deny`, `ew-allow-same-namespace`), run when the target is saved or checked and before dependency provisioning. Expose it as `AppRuntimeTargetResolver.ensureNamespace(workId)` in CONTRACTS §3. Make APW-07 providers check for `ew-allow-same-namespace` rather than `ew-allow-deps`. Update ACCEPTANCE E2E-05 event order.

gaps.title: First Deployment deadlocks: dependency providers need a namespace and policies that APW-06 only creates during a Deployment, and a Deployment waits for ready dependencies
gaps.evidence: APW-07 plan.md:533-535 says the provider checks that `ew-default-deny` and `ew-allow-deps` exist before provisioning and otherwise fails with `namespacePoliciesMissing`. T19 (tasks.md:263-264) tests that. APW-06 plan.md:713 says `namespace` is 'Frozen at first Deployment', and the five policies are drawn by the App renderer inside deployApp (APW-06 plan.md:301, 425-436). APW-06 refuses a Deployment on `dependency_not_ready` (APW-06 plan.md:493), and APW-07 FR-26/FR-41 require dependencies to be ready before the first Deployment. The result is a circular wait. Two more problems: `ew-allow-deps` in APW-06 only allows egress to outside addresses (APW-06 plan.md:434), so it is not what keeps other pods away from the dependency pods (T19's reason for ACC-07-14 is wrong). And with `isolation: false` no policies are drawn at all (APW-06 plan.md:436), so FR-38 cannot hold and every provider would fail.
gaps.proposedFix: Add a CONTRACTS §3 row owned by APW-06 for a runtime target preparation step. On target save or connection check it fixes and stores the namespace, and an `app-cluster-op` op (e.g. `prepare-namespace`) applies the namespace, the policies and the LimitRange before any dependency is provisioned. Change APW-07 plan §4.9 and T19 to check the policies APW-06 really draws (`ew-default-deny` + `ew-allow-same-namespace`). Add a dependency-scoped ingress policy `dep-<kind>` that admits only the app's pod labels, and define what happens when isolation is off (draw `dep-<kind>` anyway, or show a warning). Add the matching APW-06 task.

gaps.title: No SMTP dependency can work on Ever Works Apps; Cal.diy and the fixture (ACC-E2E-10b) both require one
gaps.evidence: Cal.diy (works.yml L93) and app-fixture-hello (L66) declare `smtp: { required: true }`. On the tier, LG-08 (APW-10 spec L190) and FR-21 (L270-273) refuse outbound mail ports 25, 465 and 587. APW-07 Wave 2 providers are only managed-postgres, managed-redis and managed-object-storage (FR-51 L352-354; plan L96-97). gaps.title: Upstream commits are built and deployed to the user's app with no human review
gaps.evidence: APW-02 S4/FR-35 fast-forwards a fork with no own commits straight onto the tracked branch; FR-37 checks only the license gate. APW-05 FR-11 builds every push to the tracked branch. The APW-06 plan §7.2 (line 712) defaults `targetSettings.autoDeploy: true`, and deploys run `pre-deploy` migrate jobs against the app's data. gaps.proposedFix: Add a per-App-Work setting 'Upstream updates: open a pull request (default) | fast-forward automatically'. gaps.title: Unverified whether any workflow runs on a fresh fork at all; the whole Build chain on a fork depends on it
gaps.evidence: The fork probe (ACCEPTANCE §6.2 L1404) measured only `GET actions/permissions → enabled: true`. It never pushed a new workflow file to a fork of a repository that already had workflows and observed a run. GitHub forks of repositories that contain workflows may show a 'workflows aren't being run on this forked repository' gate until the owner enables them. APW-02 FR-26 (spec L295) forbids hygiene from enabling any workflow, and APW-05 S15 handles only 'Actions disabled for the repository'. If the gate applies, `.github/workflows/ever-works-build.yml` never runs on a Cal.diy fork (which inherits many workflows), so no Build, Deployment or checks happen. ACC-E2E-02 asserts '0 Actions minutes' and never exercises a Build on a fresh fork.
gaps.proposedFix: Run a live probe: fork a small repository that has workflows, commit a new push-triggered workflow through the API, and record whether it runs and whether `PUT actions/workflows/{id}/enable` is required. If a gate exists, allow APW-02 hygiene (or APW-05 prepare) to enable exactly `ever-works-build.yml` (amend FR-26), and add an ACC assertion that the first Build on a fresh fork starts.

gaps.title: Step runner has no transitions for the no-change, not-runnable and question outcomes, and no option-to-effect table
gaps.evidence: The output contract allows outcome no-change | not-runnable | question (plan.md:421), but §2.3 (plan.md:152-173) and the step table §2.5 (plan.md:196-205) only handle guard red and green. FR-6 (spec.md:198-199) says a no-change run 'may end with no pull request when verification is green', but no ref to build and no resulting status are defined. plan.md:694-697 uses fixedOptions(reason) with option ids retry, optional, verify-on-cluster, accept-build-only, raise-cap, choose:<n>, stop, but gives no mapping from the 9 APP_PROVISIONING_QUESTION_REASONS to options. Effects are also undefined: who edits the spec for 'optional'; what status and verified value 'accept-build-only' gives; what 'verify-on-cluster' does in P1, where the cluster target only arrives in P2 (T34). T18's table test (tasks.md:239-253) cannot be written without these.

verify.refinedFix: 1) plan.md §2.5: add a table after the step table, "Run outcome → step, status, effect": - proposal: as today (guard → writer push → open PR once → validate …). - no-change, no proposal pushed yet: proposal step `skipped`. Validate, build (`startBuild` verify mode on `baseSha`), boot and smoke run on the default-branch head, and the attempt is counted as usual. Green: no PR comment, evidence goes on the run and the card only, `status: merged`, `verified: true`, `prNumber: null`, Task → `done` via TaskTransitionService (in_progress→done is allowed), Activity `succeeded`. Red: the normal iterate path. - no-change after a proposal was pushed: re-verify the current `headSha`. This counts as an attempt, the normal succeeded path applies, and a repeat fingerprint asks (FR-36). - not-runnable: nothing pushed, no attempt consumed. The analysis step is `failed` and later steps are `skipped`. `status: failed`, `failureReason: not-runnable`, report stored on the run for "View report". An already-open PR gets a final comment and stays open. - question: `status: needs_input` with reason = `question.reason`, `questionsAsked += 1`, no attempt consumed, current step `blocked`. If the questions ceiling is already reached: `failed/could-not-verify`. Also add matching `alt` branches to the §2.3 sequence diagram. 2) plan.md §7.7: replace the bare option-id list with two tables. (a) Reason → options, in order, ≤ 4: - attempts-spent / repeated-failure: `retry` · `accept-build-only` (only when this attempt's build passed and it failed at boot or smoke) · `stop` - missing-required-value (agent question or boot `blocked`): `retry` · `optional` · `stop` - runner-capacity: `verify-on-cluster` (P2 only, and only when the App Work's runtime target is your-cluster) · `accept-build-only` · `stop` - token-cap / runner-minute-cap: `raise-cap` · `stop` - multiple-apps, or agent-asked with candidates: `choose:0..n-1`, plus `stop` only when n ≤ 3 (the card's Cancel stays available) - agent-asked without candidates / safety-rail: `retry` · `stop` (b) Option id → row patch, next event, resume: - Every non-stop answer: `attemptBudget = min(attemptBudget + 2, 9)`, clear `openInboxItemId`. - `retry`: `status: running`; resume the run with the answer. If the agent then returns no-change, the current head is re-verified. - `optional`: resume the run with the variable name (names only, taken from the blocked boot result or the question). The agent sets that prompt to `required: false` through a normal proposal; the platform never edits the spec. - `raise-cap`: §6.4 approval flow; on approval the cap is raised and `answered` is dispatched. - `choose:<n>`: resume the run with the candidate read back from the Inbox item's option label, fenced as untrusted. - `verify-on-cluster` (P2): record a cluster pin for the next attempt (add `verificationTargetPin varchar(16) NULL` to §3.1 and the migration). Re-run boot and smoke of the same head on the cluster, reusing the image digest; no agent run. An unreachable cluster follows the infra-retry path, then `failed/verification-infrastructure`. - `accept-build-only`: no resume. Boot and smoke steps `skipped`, evidence comment marked build-only, `status: succeeded`, Task → in_review. On merge `verified: false`, so it is not eligible for a Blueprint suggestion (FR-53). - `stop`: same as the `cancel` event (`status: cancelled`). State that option labels are keyed per reason: `question.option.<reason>.<id>`, with `choose:<n>` labelled by its candidate. 3) spec.md: - §5.3: add the edge `running ──(no change needed, verified)──► merged (verified)`. - §6: add a Succeeded (build only) headline row, e.g. "App spec built but not started or smoke-tested — review the pull request with care." with actions `Open pull request` · `Re-provision`. - §6 needs-input example: mark "Verify on my cluster instead" as applying only to the runner-capacity question on your-cluster, or drop it. - Optionally add ACC-04-39 (no-change on a valid spec verifies the default-branch head and ends merged-verified with no PR) and ACC-04-40 (accept-build-only ends unverified). 4) plan.md §9: change `question.option.<id> (7 keys)` to per-reason keys, and add `headline.succeededBuildOnly`. 5) tasks.md: - T18 named cases: no-change without a pushed proposal builds `baseSha` and ends merged-verified with Task done and no PR; not-runnable → failed/not-runnable with no attempt used; question outcome → needs_input and `questionsAsked+1`; `fixedOptions(reason)` table test for all 9 reasons, including the ≤ 4 cap with 4 candidates; each option id's row patch and resume or no-resume; `verify-on-cluster` never offered in P1. - T20: assert the optionId reaches the runner for every id. - T25/T26 (card and i18n): add the build-only headline and the per-reason option keys.

T31/T32 (tasks.md:428-451) create only the dispatchers and task shells. T13 (tasks.md:199-216) creates only the plugin functions. T58 and T60 add handlers for delete-app-work and verification only. No task creates an agent-side service that routes the ops, writes `statusSnapshot`/`clusterCheck`/`clusterFingerprint`, stores logs in a named cache and serves `GET app-logs/:requestId`, cancels a running Deployment, or performs resume ('runs phases 3 and 5 with their deadlines', spec FR-49 at spec.md:443-445; `scaleApp` in T13 only scales). Nor does any task create the `app-smoke` handler that writes `smokeResult` on the current Deployment and emits `app.smoke.*` (plan.md:633-637).
gaps.proposedFix: Add a P1.5 task: create `packages/agent/src/app-runtime/app-cluster-op.handler.ts` with one method per op, naming the runtime-state writes, the cache key and TTL for logs (worker-side cache and how the API reads it), the cancel flag read by `hooks.isCancelled`, and resume = `scaleApp('resume')` + rollout wait + in-cluster smoke. Add `app-smoke.handler.ts` as well. Give each op a unit test tied to ACC-06-31/34/35/37 and FR-49/51.

gaps.title: App Works with build.strategy image can never deploy, although the Umami golden path and the ACC-E2E-05 PR — cluster half rely on it
gaps.evidence: The plan requires a WorkBuild for every Deployment: plan.md:62-64 ('takes a digest-pinned reference from WorkBuild'), plan.md:494 (`no_green_build`), plan.md:612-613, spec FR-24 at spec.md:326-329, and T35 fires only on `app.build.succeeded`. APW-05 spec.md:166-168 and 209 (FR-3) say `image` and `none` produce no Build. APW-13-golden-paths/blueprints/umami/.works/works.yml:40-43 uses `strategy: image`. ACCEPTANCE.md:352-355 expects a deploy with no Build and `GET /marker.sha` equal to the image tag. No APW-06 task defines the image source, the `build.commitSha` value, the trigger (spec applied) or rollback candidates when there is no Build.
gaps.proposedFix: Specify the image-strategy path in plan §5.1/§5.6 and T21/T22/T24/T35: image = `spec.build.image` at the spec commit; refuse a tag-only reference (or resolve it once and record the digest); `buildId` null; `build.commitSha` = spec commit; trigger on `app.spec.applied` when `build` or `components` changed and autoDeploy is on; rollback candidates keyed by spec commit + digest; pull credential null for public images. Add precondition `image_not_pinned` and tests for each rule.

The registry host passes the §6.1 public-address guard, with a 10 s timeout. - A `@sha256` reference is checked for existence. - A tag is resolved to a digest. Record `appRender.image = { reference, digest, resolvedFromTag }` and the Deployment warning `image_not_pinned`. - 404 → `image_not_found`; 401/403 → `image_private_unsupported`; timeout or network error → `image_unresolvable`. For `image`, the referenced image must be readable from its registry without credentials. For `none`, deploy is refused (nothing to deploy). 3. FR-25: for `image`, the reference is the App spec's own `build.image` at that commit, deployed by digest. 4. FR-34: rollback of an `image` Deployment reuses its recorded digest and spec commit. 5. New scenario "Published image" and new acceptance items ACC-06-4x: - no Build and no `app.build.*` event; - a tag is resolved once and rollback reuses the digest; - a private image is refused with copy; - Ever Works Apps refuses a tag-only reference. 6. §6 copy: - "This image can't be downloaded without credentials. Ever Works deploys published images only when they are public." - "This image is referenced by tag. Pin it by digest so every Deployment runs the same image." C. APW-06 tasks.md 1. T22: for `image`, the reference comes from the spec, there is no pull block, the context has `buildCommitSha: null`, and the credential port is never called. 4. T24: a request with no `buildId`, the queue keyed by spec commit, and a rollback that carries the digest. 5. T25: the worker resolution step and `appRender.image`, with an error-code test for each registry answer. 6. T35: add `apps/api/src/app-runtime/app-spec-applied.listener.ts` and its spec, covering: - changed blocks, and blocks that change nothing that runs; - `autoDeploy` off; - target `none`; - strategy `dockerfile` ignored. 7. T39: history rows for `image` show the short digest instead of a Build link. 8. T42: the cluster half of ACC-E2E-05. D. gaps.evidence: T2 (tasks.md:55-61) says to create about 20 types 'of plan §3', but plan.md:170-265 defines only AppDeployTarget, AppDeployPhase, AppTargetRef, AppRenderInput, AppDeployHooks and AppDeployResult. AppComponentInput, AppJobInput, AppCronInput, AppSmokeInput, AppStatusSnapshot, AppStatusSpec, AppJobRunRequest, AppJobResult, AppLogRequest, AppLogTail, AppClusterCheckRequest, AppClusterCheck, AppDestroyResult, AppQuotaInput, AppLimitRangeInput, AppSmokeRun/AppSmokeResult/CheckResult, AppComponentStatus, AppFailureCode and AppLogRef have no fields. gaps.title: External SMTP/S3 refuse private addresses with no allow-list, which blocks the kind lane and self-hosted installs

gaps.title: spec.agents.requireHumanMergePaths is not in the App spec schema, so human-merge paths are rejected as unknown fields

gaps.title: App checks never run on Fleet nodes: checksPolicy and repoDeclaredCommands both default to off and no task switches them on
gaps.evidence: `Work.checksPolicy` defaults to 'off' and `repoDeclaredCommands` defaults to mode 'off' (work.entity.ts:514-546; repo-declared-commands.types.ts:157-160). task-gates.types.ts:197-213 says `off` is an execution switch that also stops `.works/works.yml` being read on the fleet path. readFleetRepoDeclaredCommands returns empty unless mode === 'allowlist' (task-workspace.service.ts:553-556), and the planner skips it when checksPolicy is off (apps/api/src/fleet/fleet-agent-task-planner.service.ts:560-577). No task changes either setting for kind `app`: T11's listener sets only taskIsolation, taskIsolationBaseBranch and taskIsolationTargetRepo (tasks.md:186-189), T13 only changes parse/admit, and T14 writes only the allow-list. So FR-14's Not admitted result and FR-16's required-check gate silently never apply on Fleet runs.
gaps.proposedFix: Pick one and specify it in plan §2.3/§2.6 and T11/T13: (a) the app-spec-applied listener sets `checksPolicy` to 'required' when the spec has a required check, and `repoDeclaredCommands.mode` to 'allowlist' (keeping the existing allow list, empty by default); or (b) App spec checks bypass these two switches for kind app. Add unit cases proving an App Work with default columns reports Not admitted and a non-green gate.

gaps.title: Check ids built as slug(name) break the repo/ prefix: repository checks could override owner checks and receive run env grants
gaps.evidence: plan.md:197-198 maps App spec checks to `TaskAcceptanceCheck` with `id = slug(name)`. packages/contracts/src/tasks/repo-declared-commands.types.ts:127-143 requires every repository-declared command id to carry `REPO_DECLARED_COMMAND_ID_PREFIX = 'repo/'`. Check ids are the merge key with owner checks, so a free id lets a repository replace or suppress an owner-authored check. The fleet node also uses the prefix as an authorship marker to withhold run env grants. fleet-agent-task-planner.service.ts:586-589 relies on the prefix for the same reason.
gaps.proposedFix: In plan §2.3 and T13, keep the `repo/` + position id produced by the existing parser. Carry the App spec `name` in `TaskAcceptanceCheck.name` for display and for matching `Ever Works check: {name}`. Add a test that an App spec check named like an owner check id cannot replace it and gets no env grants.

gaps.title: CI gate semantics the T16 test asserts need production changes no task lists: required vs advisory legs, maxGateAttempts, BLOCKED + gate-exhausted
gaps.evidence: T16 (tasks.md:277-282) creates only a test. That test requires: a failed non-required leg leaves the gate unchanged; resumes are counted against `maxGateAttempts`; exhaustion moves the Task to BLOCKED with escalation `gate-exhausted`. Current code does none of this, and T16 modifies only task-gates.ts. `deriveCiState` marks failing on any completed failure, whatever the check (packages/plugin/src/contracts/capabilities/git-provider.pr-insights.ts:43-58). The CI fix-loop budget is the platform env var TASK_CI_AUTO_RESUME_MAX_ATTEMPTS, not the Work's maxGateAttempts (packages/agent/src/config/index.ts:1590-1600; task-ci-auto-resume.ts:24-41). Exhaustion files an Inbox notice (task-ci-auto-resume.service.ts:594-598). The merge gate skips unless ciState is 'passing' (task-merge-gate.service.ts:130-132). Unverified: whether GitHub reports a failed job-level `continue-on-error` leg as a failure check run. Both APW-05 plan.md:855-856 and APW-08 plan.md:210-211 assume it gives advisory semantics. Spec S3 says 'attempt 2 of 3', but FR-17's default is 2.
gaps.proposedFix: Add Modify steps to T16 for task-pr-status.service.ts / task-ci-auto-resume(.service).ts. For App Works, classify `Ever Works check: {name}` legs using AppWorkRulesService at the PR base (a required leg failing makes ciState failing; an advisory leg is ignored), take the budget from maxGateAttempts, and on exhaustion transition to BLOCKED and record `gate-exhausted`. Record the continue-on-error conclusion as a fact to verify, with a fallback that does not depend on it. Fix S3's copy.

gaps.title: Two epics build the same CI checks job, and their trigger and env var name disagree
gaps.evidence: APW-05 T41 creates `packages/plugins/github-actions-build/src/workflow/checks-job.ts` + `checks-job.spec.ts` (APW-05 tasks.md:549-564). Its plan §4.14 says pull-request trigger only (APW-05 plan.md:838-847), and CONTRACTS.md:291 names APW-05 the owner. APW-08 T15 separately modifies `generator.ts` with its own golden `app-checks-two.yml` and triggers on 'same-repository pull requests and on the tracked branch' (tasks.md:255-270; plan.md:202-214). Within APW-08, plan §9.6 says the command goes through `env.CHECK_COMMAND` (plan.md:758), while T15 and plan §2.3 say `EW_CHECK_COMMAND_B64`. T15's run command uses a placeholder '<github-actions-build package> (package name set by APW-05 T7)', but APW-05 already names `@ever-works/github-actions-build-plugin` (APW-05 tasks.md:564).
gaps.proposedFix: Turn T15 into a dependency/verification task on APW-05 T41 (no second generator change), or move the golden into APW-05. Settle one trigger set (PR-only, or PR + tracked branch) in both epics and in R-9/CONTRACTS §3. Fix plan §9.6 to `EW_CHECK_COMMAND_B64`, and write the real package filter.

gaps.title: AppChangeGuard refuses on `truncated`, which also fires on large patches, so small dependency updates are rejected as 'over 300 files'
gaps.evidence: plan.md:245-246 calls `getCompareDiff(..., { maxFiles: 300 })` and refuses when `truncated` or `totalFiles >= 300`, using the copy 'too many files … (over 300)'. `capDiffFiles` also sets `truncated = true` when patch text exceeds `maxBytes`, whose default is 256 KiB (git-provider.pr-insights.ts:22, 86-97, 106-136). A 5-file change carrying a big lockfile patch would be refused, although lockfiles are excluded from size (FR-25) and FR-51 plans dependency-update Tasks. Spec FR-21 says 'more than 300 files' (spec.md:270-271), while the plan refuses at exactly 300. The GitHub compare API lists at most 300 files, so `>= 300` is the only detectable signal and the spec wording is wrong.
gaps.proposedFix: In plan §2.5/T17, refuse only when `totalFiles >= 300` (or files.length < totalFiles). Ignore patch truncation, or pass `maxBytes: 0` since only paths and counts are needed. Align the FR-21 wording ('300 or more files, the provider limit'). Add a guard test: few files with a huge patch → not refused.

gaps.title: Delivery tracking keys on a column read from raw spec.source.branch, which is optional, and existing App Works are never backfilled
gaps.evidence: isDeliveryTracked requires `status.baseRef === work.taskIsolationBaseBranch` (plan.md:224-228). That column is set only by the app.spec.applied listener, from `spec.source.branch` (plan.md:260-262; tasks.md:186-189). In APW-03 schema.md:117, `source.branch` is optional (default = the data repository's default branch), and schema.md:20 says defaults are never written back. With the branch omitted the column stays null and every merge completes as today, so FR-30 is silently off. provisionForRun also uses the column (task-workspace.service.ts:231-233). No task backfills App Works created between APW-01/03 landing and APW-08 P1, and the listener fires only on an effective-hash change.
gaps.proposedFix: Resolve the source branch from APW-03's `WorkAppSpecState` tracked branch (or getEffectiveSpec with defaults applied), falling back to the repository default branch. Add a one-off backfill (job or migration step) for existing kind-app Works. Add a T11/T22 test with an App spec that omits `source.branch`.

gaps.title: decideDelivery has no input table mapping Build and Deployment states to delivery states; image/auto strategies unhandled
gaps.evidence: T20 says 'the full table of plan §9.1', but plan.md:694 only says 'every state transition in spec §5.3', and plan.md:230-233 names inputs without a mapping. Several inputs are undefined: APW-06 Deployment states READY, READY + appRender.warnings, ERROR, ROLLED_BACK, CANCELED, SUPERSEDED, VERIFYING (APW-06 plan.md:622-626, 702); APW-05 Build status queued|running|succeeded|failed|cancelled|blocked with `deployable` and trigger pull_request (APW-05 plan.md:271-282); and how `smokeResult` becomes live vs live-with-warnings. Spec FR-30 names 'rollback-failed', which is not an APW-06 state. `build.strategy: image` runs no Build (APW-03 schema.md:649), and APW-08 handles only `none` (FR-32), so such Tasks stay `merged` forever. `auto` yields a Build `blocked strategyNotSupported` (APW-05 plan.md:967), which is also unmapped.
gaps.proposedFix: Add to plan §2.4 a normative table: one row per (Build status/deployable/trigger, Deployment state/warnings/smoke, target, autoDeploy, strategy) → delivery state, including image (treat like none, or close at merge), blocked, cancelled and superseded. Reference it from T20 as the test table.

gaps.title: FR-67 needs_input has no producer: safety-gate refusals never reach the Task lifecycle
gaps.evidence: `AgentRunService.evaluateSafety` turns a held or refused verdict into a tool result for the model, and the run continues (packages/agent/src/agents/agent-run.service.ts:1541-1580). No run status, event or callback carries railId/category out of the run. T46 (tasks.md:634-648) adds a pure classifier and says 'on needs_input, Task → BLOCKED' in task-transition.service.ts, but no task modifies agent-run.service.ts, the run finisher or the fleet result path to produce that signal. gaps.proposedFix: Name the producer in plan §2.3/T46, for example: AgentRunService records the first non-stop refused/held verdict on the run row (or ends the run with a stop reason), and the run finisher (cloud) and fleet-agent-task-reconciler (Fleet) call classifyAppWorkRunStop. Add those files to T46 with a test from a refused tool call to a BLOCKED Task.

gaps.title: Evolve-loop and upstream-PR agents read untrusted content with unrestricted tool grants
gaps.evidence: The APW-04 plan §7.4 (lines 642-651) denies the Provisioner `sendEmail`, `searchWeb`, `messageAgent`, `notifyChannel`, `delegateToAgent`, `createSubAgent` and all MCP tools. The APW-08 and APW-09 plans and specs have no equivalent policy (searching for sendEmail, canCallExternalTools or deny finds nothing). Yet APW-08 FR-23 passes the fork's instruction files to the agent, APW-05 FR-39 passes build failure excerpts, and APW-09 passes upstream CONTRIBUTING files and reviewer comments. FR-12(b) only restricts network inside the run sandbox, while platform-side tools run outside it. The chat tools added by APW-01/04/08 (create Work, `provisionAppWork`, evolve) stay callable.
gaps.proposedFix: Define an 'App Work Task tool policy' in CONTRACTS, owned by APW-08 and consumed by APW-09. It denies outbound messaging, MCP, web fetch, sub-agents and every App Works mutation tool (create, deploy, env, target, upstream PR), allows `ask_human`, and is re-checked at dispatch the way APW-04 re-checks its grants. Add a task and extend ACC-NEG-05 to assert no tool call leaves the platform.

gaps.title: Drift: Fleet-node containment is now recorded and is weaker than APW-08's 'owner holds the blast radius' assumption
gaps.evidence: Since e5f43f44d, develop gained 5374943fd/da2208436 ('deny the model step the operator's home, and record what containment a run got'). It adds `apps/node/src/core/model-execution/isolated-home.ts` and `FleetAgentTaskContainment` in `packages/contracts/src/fleet/fleet-jobs.types.ts`, normalised by `apps/api/src/fleet/fleet-agent-task-reconciler.service.ts`. The commit states that isolation controls environment variables only, with no filesystem boundary and no egress control. A node may decline to isolate (recorded as a downgrade). Setup and acceptance checks are not isolated. APW-08 FR-12(a)/FR-13/FR-14 still admit App Work Tasks and repository-declared checks from third-party forks on a Fleet node without citing or gating on this record. The ACCEPTANCE preconditions (line 365) don't mention it either.

Otherwise stop with needs_input, or require an explicit owner opt-in that warns about the downgrade. State that checks and setup run with the operator's real home. Show the containment record on the Task's Cost or Delivery view. Cite the three new files in the plan and add an ACC for a downgraded node.

gaps.title: Mission template build-on-open-source-app targets a catalog whose schema rejects it and that the platform never reads
gaps.evidence: Validating APW-08-evolve-loop/mission-template-draft/.works/mission.yml against the live ever-works/missions schema/mission-template.schema.json fails: required slug, title, type, summary, schedule missing; additional properties version, defaults, kb, appWork, suggestedGoals. gaps.title: Squash base is the fork's branch head, not the upstream commit the prepared branch was cut from, so every preparation is refused
gaps.evidence: tasks.md:221-223 (T15) and plan.md:150-153 pass `squashOnto: task.baseSha`. `task.baseSha` is written by TaskWorkspaceService.provisionForRun (task-workspace.service.ts:229-260) from the handle's baseSha. Both workspace plugins set it to `rev-parse refs/remotes/origin/<baseRef>`, the Work's tracked branch (local-workspace.plugin.ts:340-347, sandbox-workspace.plugin.ts:165-172), and APW-08 sets that branch to spec.source.branch (APW-08 plan.md §2.6). That commit is the fork head with its customisations. The branch `upstream-pr/...` is cut from the upstream head, so T13's `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> HEAD` check (tasks.md:186-187) refuses. The plan §3.1 column list (plan.md:187-216) also has no column holding the upstream base sha. The finalize empty check and changedFiles (local-workspace.plugin.ts:452-460) are measured against the wrong base too.
gaps.proposedFix: Add a column `upstreamBaseSha varchar(64) NULL` to plan §3.1 and T7. In T15, modify `provisionForRun` (not only `finalizeRun`) so a Task bound to an upstream_pull_requests row provisions with `baseRef = row.headBranch`, making baseSha the upstream head. Pass `squashOnto: row.upstreamBaseSha`. Add a T15 test asserting the squash base equals the sha passed to createBranchFromSha.

gaps.title: Review follow-up Tasks (`upstream-pr-update:<id>`) are never routed out of the normal finalize and open a same-repository PR
gaps.evidence: T15 (tasks.md:221-223) adds the finalize branch only for `upstream-pr:*` labels. The follow-up label `upstream-pr-update:<id>` (plan.md:170, tasks.md:355) does not start with `upstream-pr:`. T26 (tasks.md:351-359) modifies only the controller, never task-workspace.service.ts. The follow-up Task therefore reaches `simulateMerge` against the fork base and then `openPullRequestForBranch` (task-workspace.service.ts:1235-1272), opening a PR inside the fork. APW-08 T17's AppChangeGuard also runs on it.
gaps.proposedFix: Extend T26 with **Modify** `packages/agent/src/tasks-domain/task-workspace.service.ts`: a Task bound to `row.followUpTaskId` calls `UpstreamReviewFollowUpService.onFollowUpFinalized` (no squash, no simulateMerge, no same-repo PR, placed before APW-08's guard). Refuse it in `finalizeRemotePush`. Add a spec asserting no createPullRequest call for the follow-up Task.

gaps.title: No contract for how the preparation Agent reports its result, and FR-12's check limits have no enforcer
gaps.evidence: skill-draft/SKILL.md:79-81 says 'Report a structured result: status, claRequired with link, projectLimit, title, body, checks[]'. Nothing says where that report lives (final message, workspace file, tool call), its schema or size caps, or how `onPreparationFinalized` reads and validates it. A file in the workspace would itself land in the diff. T16 (tasks.md:233-236) consumes 'the project's smaller stated limit reported by the run' and 'flags aiNotAccepted/dcoRequired/CLA'. plan §3.1 (plan.md:206-209) has no column for the CLA agreement URL the Inbox 'Open the agreement' needs, nor for the doesNotPort missing-pieces list (S21, up to 10). FR-12 (spec.md:208-212) requires at most 10 commands, 30 min each and 60 min total, with results attached, but no component runs or times the checks. They are self-reported by an Agent reading untrusted repository text (README rule 9).
gaps.proposedFix: Define `UpstreamPreparationReport` in `packages/contracts/src/apps/upstream-pull-request.types.ts`: status union, title ≤ 72, body ≤ 8,000, claUrl, projectLimitLines, aiPolicyQuote ≤ 300, missingPieces ≤ 10, checks[] ≤ 10. Name the delivery vehicle (e.g. the run's final structured output, or `.ever-works/upstream-pr-report.json` removed before squash and excluded from the diff), with validation and a refusal on a malformed report. Add columns `claUrl` and `missingPieces`. State that check evidence is agent-reported and labelled as such on the approval, or add a platform-run check step with the FR-12 limits.

gaps.title: The PR-lane e2e specs (T24) and ACC-NEG-06 cannot run: the fake GitHub lacks the endpoints and nothing can complete a preparation run
gaps.evidence: plan.md:576 says '(provider mocked at the plugin boundary)', which a Playwright spec against a running API cannot do. The only non-production hook is APW-13's fake GitHub, whose REST subset (APW-13 plan.md:405-411) has no POST/PATCH/DELETE git/refs, no interaction-limits, no pulls/:n reviews or comments, and no check-runs/statuses. T24's run command (tasks.md:337) omits `EVER_WORKS_E2E_FAKES=1`. Neither epic defines how a preparation Agent run reaches `awaiting_approval` in a PR lane (no fake pipeline, no seed route). ACC-NEG-06 (ACCEPTANCE.md:659) requires 'an awaiting_approval proposal seeded' with no named seeding mechanism.
gaps.proposedFix: Add an APW-09 task, or an APW-13 task referenced by T24, that extends the fake GitHub with `POST /repos/:o/:r/git/refs`, `PATCH|DELETE /repos/:o/:r/git/refs/heads/*`, `GET /repos/:o/:r/interaction-limits`, `GET /repos/:o/:r/pulls/:n`, `/pulls/:n/reviews`, `/pulls/:n/comments`, and `/commits/:ref/check-runs|statuses`. Define a non-production seed for `upstream_pull_requests` rows plus an approval proposal (e.g. via `/_control/seed` plus a test-only API guarded like EVER_WORKS_E2E_FAKES). Add `EVER_WORKS_E2E_FAKES=1` to T24's command.

gaps.title: The extra-files acknowledgement (S22/FR-10) is enforced only in the UI; the Inbox reply and approvals API bypass it
gaps.evidence: spec.md:151-153 (S22): **Approve and open** stays disabled until **I've reviewed the extra files** is ticked. plan.md:453 and T21 (tasks.md:311-312) gate it only in `UpstreamApprovalReview`. Approvals are also decided by the Inbox reply (inbox.service.ts:802-816 calls `approvals.decide` directly) and by `POST /api/agent-approvals/:id/approve` (plan.md:385). Neither knows about the tick. No column or endpoint records the acknowledgement, and the open job's re-checks (plan.md:432) do not include it.
gaps.proposedFix: Add a column `extraFilesAcknowledgedAt timestamptz NULL` and a route `POST /api/works/:id/upstream-pull-requests/:prId/acknowledge-extra-files`. The open job and listener refuse (row stays `awaiting_approval`, Activity note) when `diffStats.extraFiles.length > 0` and the acknowledgement is null. Alternatively, create the approval proposal only after the acknowledgement. Add unit and controller tests.

gaps.title: The enable toggle (T20) depends on a non-deterministic agent Task and has no persisted pending state
gaps.evidence: plan.md:389-392 and T20 (tasks.md:286-294): toggling files APW-08 `POST /api/works/:id/evolve`, which creates an Agent Task that edits `.works/works.yml`. That endpoint returns `409 agentRequired` / `noIsolatedRuntime` (APW-08 tasks.md:389-395), which T20 does not handle. APW-03 FR-26 (APW-03 spec.md:246) marks any Task PR changing `upstreamPullRequests` as needing a person. The fallback, 'APW-03's App spec write path if it offers one', does not exist: grep of APW-03 finds no write route. 'Reports pending until the spec change merges' has no storage: plan.md:230-232 says there is no other schema change.
gaps.proposedFix: Specify a deterministic platform-authored change: a branch plus `commitFiles` (APW-03 CONTRACTS §3) setting `spec.upstreamPullRequests.enabled`, then a setup PR against the tracked branch, reusing APW-03's blueprint-apply pattern (R-4 link = PR). Persist the pending PR (e.g. a small `work_upstream_pr_settings` table or APW-02 `WorkUpstreamState` field via CONTRACTS). Define the 409 / no-agent behaviour and the web copy.

gaps.title: Quarantine 'isolation' adds an empty NetworkPolicy, which cannot block traffic other policies allow, and LG-18 only checks a timestamp
gaps.evidence: plan.md:184-186, step (1): 'apply namespace `quarantine` NetworkPolicy denying all ingress and egress'. plan.md:331: `quarantine` 'Selects all pods; ingress [], egress []'. The tenant template (plan.md:326-330) keeps `allow-dns`, `allow-edge-ingress`, `allow-internet-egress` and `allow-tenant-data` on the same pods. Kubernetes NetworkPolicies only add allowed traffic: a policy with no rules cannot take away traffic another policy allows, so quarantined pods keep internet egress and edge ingress until they scale to zero. Removal (§2.6, step 1) uses the same mechanism. LG-18 (plan.md:393) and T7 (tasks.md:139-149) prove isolation only by `status.quarantine.networkIsolatedAt`, a timestamp the controller writes itself, and by call order on a fake API. The default kind CNI used by T11 does not enforce NetworkPolicy at all. The gate can go green while isolation does nothing.
gaps.proposedFix: Pick an isolation that works. Either give every `allow-*` policy the podSelector `hosting.ever.works/quarantined NotIn ["true"]` and have the sequencer label pod templates, or delete the `allow-*` policies on quarantine and re-create them from the tenant template on release, recording that in status. Add a real probe to LG-18: a canary pod kept alive through the isolation window must see the public control and edge path refused within 15 s (reason `QUARANTINE_NOT_ISOLATING`). Update T4's golden files and T7's assertions. Install a CNI that enforces NetworkPolicy in T11's kind job and assert egress is refused there.

gaps.title: APW-06's renderer output for ever-works-apps conflicts with APW-10's tenant template, and no task maps Work.spec back to AppRenderInput
gaps.evidence: T6 (tasks.md:124-131) says to render 'through APW-06's App renderer library' but not which of its objects to keep. APW-06's renderer, for ever-works-apps, produces: namespace `ew-<slug>-<8 hex>` (APW-06 plan.md:291); NetworkPolicies `ew-default-deny`, `ew-allow-same-namespace`, `ew-allow-egress`, etc. (:301); LimitRange with a 1 CPU/512Mi default limit and 2 CPU/4Gi max; ResourceQuota 2/4 CPU, 4Gi/6Gi, 20 pods, 20Gi (:319-325). APW-10 instead creates namespace `ewa-<20 hex>`, its own policies, a LimitRange `defaults` with a 500m/512Mi default limit (plan.md:324-334), and FR-47 Starter quota 1/2 CPU, 2/4 GiB, 10 pods (spec.md:372-375). Applying both gives two quotas, two LimitRanges, and an extra `ew-allow-egress` that widens the egress deny list (see G02). The controller must rebuild an AppRenderInput from Work.spec (it needs `env.values`, `policy`, `ingress`, `hosts.previous`, `deploymentShort`; APW-06 plan.md:195-235), but no task names that reverse mapping; T26 maps only the forward direction. APW-06's port `podPolicy()` is synchronous and takes no workId (APW-06 plan.md:887), yet APW-10 plan.md:582 says it comes 'from the Work's profile'. T3's controller package.json (tasks.md:86-88) lists only `@kubernetes/client-node`, but the renderer is exported by `@ever-works/k8s-plugin`, which peer-depends on `@ever-works/plugin`, and T1 expects `@ever-works/contracts` to resolve.
gaps.proposedFix: In plan §3.4 and T6, state that the controller uses only APW-06's workload builders (Deployments, Services, Ingress, Jobs, CronJobs, PVCs, env Secret) and discards the renderer's Namespace, ServiceAccount, LimitRange, ResourceQuota and NetworkPolicy objects; tenancy objects come only from `tenant-template.ts`. Add `apps/apps-tier-controller/src/render/work-to-render-input.ts` with a golden round-trip test against T26's mapper. Change the APW-06 port to `podPolicy(workId): Promise<…>`, or state that the platform-side values are informational only. Add `@ever-works/k8s-plugin`, `@ever-works/plugin` and `@ever-works/contracts` (workspace:*) to T3's package.json.

gaps.title: The ever-works-apps plugin leaves out APW-06's App plugin methods and the owner states APW-06 must show
gaps.evidence: APW-06 plan.md:253-264 defines `deployApp(input, credential, hooks): AppDeployResult` (phases, job results, in-cluster and public smoke, rollback), plus `scaleApp` (owner pause/resume), `getAppLogs` and `checkAppCluster`. APW-10 T26 (tasks.md:423-435) implements only `supportsApps`, `deployApp → applyWork` (which returns `{ generation }`), `getAppStatus`, `runAppJob` (via an unnamed 'spec job trigger annotation') and `destroyApp`. `Work.spec.desiredState` has no paused state (plan.md:233). Work.status has no job or smoke results (plan.md:249-261). The platform Role has no `pods/log` (plan.md:292-311), so owner logs on the tier are impossible. `grep quarantin` over APW-06 finds nothing, yet T26's Done-when and ACC-10-35 need APW-06 to record 'Cancelled — quarantined'. T30 (tasks.md:497) mounts a banner in APW-06's deploy page, but APW-06 never mentions `AppsTierQuarantineBanner` or `GET /api/me/apps-tier`. APW-06 tasks.md:635 and :643 expect a tier refusal code `isolation_not_enforced`, which APW-10's refusal list (plan.md:265-268) never emits. There is no mapping from APW-10 refusal codes to APW-06 AppFailureCode.
gaps.proposedFix: Add a plan §5.2 table defining the ever-works-apps behaviour of every IDeploymentPluginAppMembers method. Add `desiredState: paused` with recorded replicas for `scaleApp`. Either return `getAppLogs` as unsupported with code `logs_unavailable_on_tier`, or add a `LogRequest` CR the controller fulfils. Map `deployApp` hooks onto polled Work.status phases and define job/smoke result fields in status. Add a table mapping APW-10 refusal codes to APW-06 AppFailureCode, including `quarantined` → outcome `cancelled`. Add CONTRACTS rows for the owner banner mount and `/api/me/apps-tier` consumption, and list matching APW-06 cross-epic tasks.

gaps.title: No task implements probe LG-17 or the platform half of LG-19, and the LG-18 drill handshake is undefined
gaps.evidence: T9 (tasks.md:163-178) runs zone probes for LG-02…LG-11, LG-13, LG-14, LG-19 (zone part) and LG-22. T16 (tasks.md:262-266) runs platform probes for LG-12, LG-15, LG-16, LG-18, LG-20, LG-21 and LG-23. Nothing runs LG-17 (plan.md:392: canary custom hostname `active` through edge-hostnames plus a dry-run Ingress with an unregistered host); T24 only creates the capability. The platform half of LG-19 (a `test:true` AbuseSignal imported within 120 s) is also unassigned. FR-3 requires every P2 item to pass, so the P2 gate can never be green. LG-18 is split between a 'zone part' (T9) and platform quarantine 'via the T17 service path' (T16), but no protocol says who writes and reads the marker or when the platform may quarantine, and T16 is ordered before T17. LG-21 (plan.md:396) looks for rows with 'actor `system:self-check`', but `apps_tier_quarantines` (plan.md:444) has no actor column.
gaps.proposedFix: Add LG-17 to T16: create or reuse a canary custom hostname through EdgeHostnamesFacade, with reasons CUSTOM_HOSTNAME_NOT_ACTIVE and UNREGISTERED_HOST_ADMITTED, plus the dry-run in T9. Add the LG-19 import check to T16. Define the drill as SelfCheck status sub-phases (`markerWritten` → platform quarantines → `quarantineObserved` → platform releases → `markerVerified`) with the platform polling for each, and move LG-18 after T17 or make T16 depend on it. Change LG-21 to match `source = 'self-check'`.

gaps.title: Custom domains on Ever Works Apps: the edge-hostnames capability has no consumer and no storage
gaps.evidence: CONTRACTS.md:296 lists APW-06 as the consumer of `edge-hostnames`, and plan.md:608-614 says 'APW-06's custom-domain flow for target Ever Works Apps calls it through a facade and passes customHostnameRef'. `grep -rn "edge-hostname|EdgeHostname|customHostnameRef"` over APW-06-app-runtime/ and APW-13-golden-paths/ finds nothing. T24 (tasks.md:387-401) builds only the interface, the provider and the facade. No task: stores the edge hostname id or status per custom domain; shows the owner the `ownershipValidation` record or `fallbackTarget` (the CNAME to set); polls until active; calls `deleteCustomHostname` on removal or domain delete; or sets `Work.spec.hosts[].customHostnameRef`. ACC-10-31's live half (E2E-10 b) cannot be built.
gaps.proposedFix: Add an APW-10 P2 task (or an APW-06 task named in CONTRACTS) for `packages/agent/src/apps-tier/apps-tier-custom-hostname.service.ts`. Persistence: either a new table `apps_tier_custom_hostnames` (`id`, `workId`, `host` varchar(253) unique, `edgeHostnameId` varchar(64), `status`, `certificateStatus`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`) in migration slot 03, or additive columns on WorkCustomDomain. Also: a gate-watch poll step, owner copy for the TXT validation and CNAME target, deletion on removal, and backup classification (R-25).

gaps.title: Hosting prices go into the wrong file, their units don't match the metered units, and nothing actually charges credits
gaps.evidence: T28 (tasks.md:465-467) adds 'the five hosting.* price keys at 0' to `packages/agent/src/usage/credit-price-list.ts`, but that file only defines the price-list interface. Prices live in `packages/agent/src/subscriptions/billing/credit-pricebook.ts`, whose frozen VERSION_1 (lines 57, 67) never changes; its header says a new price means a new version. The `group` of a price entry must be one of CREDIT_PRICE_GROUPS = research|data|tools|models (`packages/contracts/src/billing/meter.types.ts:92`), which has no hosting group. Metered units are cpu_core_seconds, memory_mib_hours, egress_mib and storage_gib_hours (plan.md:448), but the price keys are cpu_core_hour, memory_gib_hour, egress_gib and storage_gib_month (plan.md:533-536), with no conversion defined. `priceFor` rounds units to whole numbers (credit-pricebook.ts:113). The price key is built from capability and operation (`usage-meter-classifier.ts:92-95`) and a missing payer is recorded as `unconfirmed`, yet the plan passes neither operation nor payer. Under the default settlement mode (`provider_cost`), only Agent runs are debited, so the 'credits charged' on daily receipts (spec FR-51, §6.3) never leave anyone's balance.
gaps.proposedFix: Point T28 at `credit-pricebook.ts`: add VERSION_2 with an effectiveFrom date, add `hosting` to CREDIT_PRICE_GROUPS, and update `credit-pricebook.spec.ts`. Define integer billing units with a conversion and a carried remainder on AppsTierUsageWindow (e.g. core-seconds/3600 → cpu_core_hour). Pass `operation` and `payer: platform` to `PluginUsageService.record`. Specify the debit: e.g. the daily-receipt job debits the credit ledger with idempotency key `apps-tier:<workId>:<YYYY-MM-DD>`. Alternatively, state explicitly that P2 records at 0 credits with no debit until the owner sets prices.

gaps.title: In P1, zone admission would refuse the canary and probe workloads the self-check needs
gaps.evidence: Probe Jobs use 'same image, `probe` entrypoint' (plan.md:132), and T10 pushes that image to the organisation registry (tasks.md:185-186). The zone policy `tenant-image-source` (plan.md:351) requires every tenant image to be `<zone registry>/t-<namespace id>/…@sha256`, and signature verification (plan.md:356) requires the zone promotion key. Canaries use the same tenant template with no exemption (D-F, ACC-10-06). Copying, scanning and signing images (T23) only arrives in P2 (tasks.md:371-385), and T6's reconcile has no P1 promotion step. So T9's probe Jobs and T22's P1 self-check and quarantine drill on a real zone would be refused. No canary application image (HTTPS for LG-16, a DB client for LG-14, marker storage for LG-18) is named, and nothing says how P2-only items (LG-13 promotion half, LG-16, LG-17, LG-20) are reported during a P1 run.
gaps.proposedFix: Move a minimal copy-and-sign promotion into P1 (T6 or a new T6a). Specify a controller startup step that promotes its own image and a named canary image (built by T10 from `apps/apps-tier-controller/canary/`) into each canary's `t-<id>` space. Name the canary image's endpoints in plan §3.7. State the outcome P2-only items get in a P1 run (e.g. `inconclusive`, reason `PHASE_NOT_ENABLED`) so ACC-10-02 can be observed at T22.

gaps.title: Owner decisions and a staging zone block the P1 and P2 ship gates
gaps.evidence: spec.md:618-629 has six open [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] items: where the tier runs, which apex domain, prices, sandbox compatibility, who handles abuse reports, and retention after removal. T22 (tasks.md:354-363) needs 'a staging zone provided by the private operations plan', which depends on README §8 question 1. LG-15/LG-16 and T32 need the apex domain, whose Public Suffix List listing 'takes weeks' (spec.md:620-621). FR-39's Medium-signal queue needs a named person or rota. T32's Done-when requires the owner's approval with these answered.
gaps.proposedFix: The owner answers README §8 questions 1-3 and spec §9 (hosting location, apex domain, credit prices for Starter/Standard, policy for apps incompatible with the sandbox, abuse rota and response target, retention against the terms of service), and operations provides the staging zone. Then record the answers in spec §9 and README §8.

gaps.title: Managed hosting spend has no out-of-credits or lapsed-subscription behaviour, no spend cap and no estimate
gaps.evidence: APW-10 FR-35 (spec line 329) checks for an active paid subscription only when deploying. FR-49/50/51 charge credits from hourly usage into a daily receipt. Nothing says what happens to running App Works, volumes or databases when credits reach zero or the subscription lapses: no grace period, scale-to-zero or notice. There is no per-App-Work or per-account monthly cap and no cost estimate before choosing Ever Works Apps. Prices remain an open question (line 622). Auto-deploy on the managed tier is also open (APW-06 spec line 735).
gaps.proposedFix: Owner decides: grace period, then pause workloads (data kept for N days, see XC-13), notices at 80%/100% of the balance, an optional monthly cap per App Work, and a pre-deploy estimate from the quota profile. APW-10 adds FRs, tasks and ACCs.

gaps.title: Tenant data retention and erasure on the managed tier has no owner, and backups are never deleted
gaps.evidence: APW-10 FR-28 (spec lines 298-304): without 'Also delete stored data', data is 'retained for 30 days and removed only by a separate, explicit operator action outside this epic', and 'Backups are never deleted by a removal'. Retention is an open question (line 628). APW-07's open question (spec lines 628-629) says storage beyond 30 days after deletion is billed. Neither epic defines backup expiry, operator access to tenant databases, owner data export (a dump of the app's database or bucket), processing terms, or erasure of end-user personal data held by hosted apps.
gaps.proposedFix: Add a data lifecycle section to APW-10 and APW-07: an erasure job with an owner and an SLA, a backup retention window and deletion after erasure, an owner export flow, an operator access policy with audit, and a legal-review item on the launch gate (new LG entry). Owner and legal confirm the durations.

gaps.title: Managed-tier desired state cannot express Deployment phase order, in-cluster smoke or authScheme
gaps.evidence: On the managed tier APW-06 only hands desired state to the tier (R-5; T46 tasks L629-647), and the zone controller 'ensures namespace → promotion → renderer + overlays → applies' (APW-10 plan L152-155). `Work.spec` (plan L229-248) has jobs and cron but no smoke checks, no rule that pre-deploy jobs run before rollout or first-deploy jobs before hosts are published, and no status for job or smoke results. `cron[].http` lacks `authScheme`, although CONTRACTS C2 (L29-30) applies it to cron. APW-06 FR-26 rows 2-7 and S6 (setup before exposure, in-cluster smoke decides rollback) have no owner on Ever Works Apps. Cal.diy's bootstrap-admin-before-exposure and its `raw` cron auth would not hold there.
gaps.proposedFix: Extend `Work.spec` with `smoke[]`, `cron[].http.authScheme` and job `when` semantics. Make the controller's reconcile phases normative (pre-deploy jobs → rollout → first-deploy jobs → in-cluster smoke → route hosts at the edge → post-deploy jobs → CronJobs), report `status.jobs[]`, `status.smoke[]` and the phase, and have APW-06 map them to Deployment states. Add LG or controller integration tests.

gaps.title: User-apps apex domain, Public Suffix List entry, DNS zone and tier edge do not exist
gaps.evidence: README section 8 question 2 is unanswered (<apps-domain> placeholder). APW-10 spec's open question notes the Public Suffix List listing takes weeks and gates LG-15; LG-16 needs a wildcard certificate on a separate edge. R-16 Wave 1 subdomains need EVER_WORKS_APPS_DOMAIN, EVER_WORKS_APPS_DNS_ZONE_ID and EVER_WORKS_APPS_DNS_API_TOKEN. gaps.proposedFix: Owner chooses and registers the apex; file the PSL pull request early (it requires a verification TXT record); create the zone and a zone-scoped DNS token per environment; record everything in the private operations repository and answer README question 2.

gaps.title: Legal and policy drafts for hosting user apps are missing (terms, acceptable use, abuse and copyright takedown)
gaps.evidence: The program contains no terms-of-service addendum, acceptable-use policy, abuse or copyright takedown process, trademark display policy or privacy/subprocessor delta for hosting user apps. LG-19 requires an attested abuse contact and acceptable-use policy; APW-10 spec asks who owns abuse handling and to confirm retention against the terms of service. The platform already has a terms-acceptance subsystem (GET /terms/required, migration 1785000000000-CreateTermsAcceptance) but no epic registers an App Works hosting document. licenses.yml attestation texts and community-build trademark notices also need wording review.
gaps.proposedFix: Draft docs/specs/features/app-works/policies-draft/ with a hosting terms addendum, acceptable-use policy, abuse and copyright takedown process (intake, response targets, mapping to APW-10 FR-41 quarantine categories), trademark display policy and a names-only subprocessor delta, each marked for counsel review; add an APW-10 task registering the hosting terms as a required document before Ever Works Apps eligibility.

gaps.title: Ever Works Apps isolated tier infrastructure is only a private draft plan with open owner decisions
gaps.evidence: APW-10 T22 and T32 need a staging zone provided by the private operations plan. That plan exists only as a draft on a research branch of the private operations repository, with owner decisions open (where the tier runs, procurement, separate edge account); nothing is provisioned, so LG-01 to LG-25 cannot pass and Wave 2 cannot open. No infrastructure specifics are repeated here.
gaps.proposedFix: Owner answers README question 1 and the private plan's decisions; merge the plan in the private operations repository and schedule the zone build before APW-10 P1's ship gate.

gaps.title: Wave 1 App Works get a tile address under the platform's own domain; ManagedHostRootResolver has no contract and no owning task
gaps.evidence: APW-11 plan.md:412-422 and tasks.md:133-137 say resolveLauncherAddress builds `<managedSubdomain>.<managedRoot>` through a ManagedHostRootResolver token that defaults to EVER_WORKS_DOMAIN, with the App-aware binding left to 'APW-06 P2' (plan.md:766-771, 808-809; tasks.md:400-401). APW-06 plan.md:770-784 and R-16 do this in Wave 1 P1 instead: an App Work on Your cluster gets `SubdomainAllocator.allocate(work, appsDnsOps)`, so the label in `works.managedSubdomain` belongs to `<EVER_WORKS_APPS_DOMAIN>` and is 'Never a label under EVER_WORKS_DOMAIN'. Because FR-16 ranks the managed subdomain above the deployment address, a live Wave 1 App Work's tile would open `<label>.<EVER_WORKS_DOMAIN>`, a wrong host under the platform's parent domain (breaks README D10). No CONTRACTS.md row names ManagedHostRootResolver, and grep for 'ManagedHostRootResolver|launcher|APW-11' in APW-06-app-runtime/plan.md and tasks.md finds nothing, so no epic implements the binding.
gaps.proposedFix: Add a CONTRACTS.md §3 row for the managed-host-root port (owner APW-06, consumer APW-11), or have APW-11 read the App Work's published primary host from APW-06 (AppHostsService primary / WorkAppRuntimeState) for kind `app`. Add an APW-06 P1 task that binds it when EVER_WORKS_APPS_DOMAIN is configured. Change APW-11 plan §4.6, §11 and T6 from 'APW-06 P2' to 'APW-06 P1', and add a T4/T6 test: an App Work whose label was allocated on the apps domain never yields a host under EVER_WORKS_DOMAIN.

gaps.title: T17 saves exposure through a path that silently drops the field and pushes a README update
gaps.evidence: tasks.md:315 says the toggle 'saves through the existing useSettings().handleUpdate path with appLauncherExposed'. At HEAD, handleUpdate (apps/web/src/components/works/detail/settings/SettingsContext.tsx:76-92) is a form-submit handler that sends the whole General form to the `updateWork` server action. That action (apps/web/src/app/actions/dashboard/works.ts:596-613) validates with a zod object listing only name/description/owner/organization/websiteTemplateId/readmeConfig, so zod strips `appLauncherExposed`. It then calls `workAPI.update` with validation.data (:638) and `workAPI.updateReadme(workId)` (:640). Following T17 as written, the choice never persists, every toggle triggers a README update on the Work's repository, and ACC-11-16 cannot pass. The web UpdateWorkDto type (apps/web/src/lib/api/work.ts:111) also lacks the field, and T17 modifies only the Work type.
gaps.proposedFix: Rewrite T17 to use a dedicated server action (for example `setWorkAppLauncherExposureAction(workId, value: boolean|null)` in apps/web/src/app/actions/dashboard/works.ts) that calls PUT /api/works/:id with only `{ appLauncherExposed }`, saves immediately on toggle (state the save and error copy), and never calls updateReadme. Add `appLauncherExposed?: boolean | null` to the web UpdateWorkDto. Add a unit test proving the body carries only that field.

gaps.title: Work settings page is manager-only, so editors and viewers never see Show in App Launcher
gaps.evidence: spec S3 and FR-20 say an editor turns the setting on and a viewer sees it read-only with 'Only editors can change this.' ACC-11-15 checks this in e2e (tasks.md:357-359). T17 mounts the control in GeneralSettings on /works/[id]/settings. At HEAD, apps/web/src/app/[locale]/(dashboard)/works/[id]/settings/page.tsx:31-33 calls notFound() unless canAccessSettings(work.userRole), and apps/web/src/lib/permissions.ts:70-71 requires MANAGER or higher. Meanwhile the API grants the change to EDITOR (packages/agent/src/services/work-ownership.service.ts:142-143 ensureCanEdit). Editors and viewers get a 404 page, so S3 by an editor and the ACC-11-15 e2e are unreachable.
gaps.proposedFix: Choose a surface that editors and viewers can reach, such as the Work Overview/Deploy tab or a read-only card outside the manager-only settings page, or state that only managers see the toggle and amend FR-20, S3 and ACC-11-15. Then update T17's mount point and test.

gaps.title: The BFF precedent drops the workspace scope, and the client cache is not keyed by Organization
gaps.evidence: plan.md:51 and 569-571 and tasks.md:265-267 describe apps/web/src/app/api/usage/costs/[section]/route.ts as forwarding 'cookie → Bearer, workspace scope header'. At HEAD that route (:36-53) sends only Authorization. The real mechanism is serverFetch (apps/web/src/lib/api/server-api.ts:108-125), which maps `x-ever-workspace` to `x-scope-slug`. Without `x-scope-slug`, the API runs the request in personal scope (apps/api/src/scope/scope-resolver.middleware.ts:43; session-scope.guard.ts:124), so ScopeContextService.getScope() never returns the Organization and Org Works are never listed. The T14 test checks only includeHidden and the token. Separately, T14 and plan.md:560-562 use one module-level 5-minute cache `{data, fetchedAt}` with no scope key, and no task closes the panel on Organization switch. After a switch within 5 minutes the panel shows the previous Organization's apps, which contradicts spec S21 (spec.md:155-157).
gaps.proposedFix: In T14, have the BFF read `x-ever-workspace` and forward `x-scope-slug` exactly as serverFetch does (or proxy through serverFetch), and add a test that asserts the header is forwarded. Key the client cache by the serialized workspace scope, close the element on scope change, and add a unit test for S21.

gaps.title: The e2e catalog fixture cannot be served by a Playwright route handler because the API fetches the catalog server-side
gaps.evidence: tasks.md:353-354 says T20 uses 'a catalog fixture served by a Playwright route handler (no network to GitHub)'. plan.md:483-499 has PlatformCatalogService in apps/api fetch platforms.json and icons from the raw GitHub host, with the repo pinned by regex `^ever-works\/[a-z0-9-]+$`. page.route intercepts only browser requests, never the API process's fetch. No env var overrides the base URL or points at a local fixture file (CONTRACTS.md:407 lists only REPO/REF/ENV/SELF_ID). Specs ACC-11-05 and ACC-11-09 in e2e therefore cannot use a fixture, and the PR lane (ACCEPTANCE §0.1: local stack, fake GitHub) would hit the real network or show the S9 error.
gaps.proposedFix: Add a non-production override honoured only when NODE_ENV !== 'production' or EVER_WORKS_E2E_FAKES=1, such as `EVER_WORKS_PLATFORM_CATALOG_BASE_URL` pointed at APW-13's fake GitHub or a fixture file path. Register it in CONTRACTS §7, cover it in T8 (refused in production), and point T20 at it. Create the fixture catalog as a draft file (see G22).

gaps.title: No way to seed live Works (READY deployment, managed subdomain, verified domain, kind app) in the PR e2e lane
gaps.evidence: plan.md:744-748 and tasks.md:355-360 need 'one live App Work + one failed Work', a live directory Work for exposure, and failed-after-success chips. No public API creates a READY WorkDeployment or a verified WorkCustomDomain: existing e2e only reads deploy state on fresh Works (apps/web/e2e/flow-work-deploy-state.spec.ts:41-46, where a refused deploy writes no state). kind `app` needs APW-01, yet plan.md:763-764 says P1 'depends on nothing'. The only direct-DB precedent is apps/web/e2e/flow-org-upgrade-from-account.spec.ts, and T20 does not name a seeding mechanism, helper file or row shapes.
gaps.proposedFix: Specify a seeding helper for T20, for example `apps/web/e2e/helpers/app-launcher-seed.ts` that writes works/work_deployments/work_custom_domains rows through the driver-aware direct-DB pattern of flow-org-upgrade-from-account.spec.ts. List the exact rows (state READY/ERROR, environment production/preview, verified, managedSubdomain, kind 'app' as a raw varchar until APW-01 lands) and name the fixture for each ACC id.

gaps.title: The flag-off e2e and flag-on e2e cannot share the PR lane, and no task turns the launcher on in e2e.yml
gaps.evidence: ACCEPTANCE.md:68 says `app-launcher` is on with EVER_WORKS_APP_LAUNCHER_ENABLED=true 'except inside app-launcher-flag-off.spec.ts'. .github/workflows/e2e.yml sets API env once for the whole prebuilt stack (env block around :330-372: SUBSCRIPTIONS_ENABLED, MAGIC_LINK_ENABLED, …) with no per-spec toggle. T20 (tasks.md:349-367) needs the API with the env unset for the flag-off spec (ACC-11-28: 'API answers 404') and set for the four other specs. No task adds the variable to e2e.yml or describes a second stack or runtime toggle.
gaps.proposedFix: Add a T20 sub-step that modifies .github/workflows/e2e.yml with `EVER_WORKS_APP_LAUNCHER_ENABLED: 'true'`. Redefine app-launcher-flag-off.spec.ts to cover the API half in the controller spec (T9, already there) plus a web-side check that does not need the API env off (for example a stubbed features.appLauncherEnabled=false through the web flag helper), or specify a dedicated flag-off shard with its own env. Update ACCEPTANCE §0.2.

gaps.title: P0 task T2 cannot finish before P1 task T6 exists (order deadlock)
gaps.evidence: tasks.md:16 says tasks run in order and tasks.md:24 says phases are ship boundaries. But T2 (P0, tasks.md:53-62) is tested with 'the Ever Works administrator Test connection (T6) against the development provider', and T6 does not exist until P1 (tasks.md:105-112). idp-options.md:193-197 also makes Status 'Decided' depend on passing Ever Works' Test connection. So P0 cannot close until P1 code ships, while P1 is gated on P0.
gaps.proposedFix: Split the gate. T2 closes on a manual read of the discovery document against plan §4.3, recorded privately. Add a P1 task after T6 that runs Test connection against the development provider. Update the idp-options §6.2 exit criteria to match.

gaps.title: No task wires the fake identity provider and oidc-identity plugin into the Playwright PR lane
gaps.evidence: ACCEPTANCE.md:69-71 requires the 'ever-id' flag on, with the oidc-identity plugin configured against the fake provider, for the ever-id-*.spec.ts PR suites. T30 (tasks.md:346-358) only creates the specs. The plugin is autoEnable:false (plan.md:408-411). The fake provider starts 'on a free port' (plan.md:765-769), but the API reads its issuer from settings or EVER_ID_ISSUER_URL, and FR-14 turns sign-in off on issuer drift. The e2e.yml API env block (.github/workflows/e2e.yml:271-286, 371) has no EVER_ID_* variables. APW-13 T13 (APW-13 tasks.md:164-170) starts only the fake GitHub. apps/web has no dependency on @ever-works/oidc-identity for the './testing' import. How ever-id-disabled.spec.ts 'turns it off per test' is not stated.
gaps.proposedFix: Add a P1 task that: starts the fake provider on a fixed port in e2e.yml and global-setup; sets EVER_ID_ISSUER_URL, EVER_ID_CLIENT_ID and EVER_ID_CLIENT_SECRET for the API; enables the plugin through the admin plugin API in a helper (apps/web/e2e/helpers/plugins.ts); adds the workspace dependency for the ./testing export; and describes how the disabled spec toggles enablement and restores it.

gaps.title: Sign-up confirm contract does not match the existing terms service, and cannot run in one transaction
gaps.evidence: plan.md:469 and 484 define POST /sign-up/confirm as { pending, acceptedTerms: string[] } (≤ 10 entries), and plan.md:583 has confirmEverIdSignUp(acceptedTerms). The real API is TermsAcceptanceService.record(userId, claims: TermsAcceptanceClaim[] {documentId, version, sha256, locale}, { method, ip, userAgent }) (apps/api/src/terms/terms-acceptance.service.ts:20, 109-117), preceded by assertClaimsArePublished (line 84). Register uses TermsAcceptanceClaimDto[] with method 'signup-checkbox' (apps/api/src/auth/dto/auth.dto.ts:112; auth.controller.ts:139, 160-163). plan.md:549-551 and T15 (tasks.md:193-195) require 'one transaction'. But record() writes through Better Auth's adapter (terms-acceptance.service.ts:156-166), and UserRepository.create is a plain repository save (user.repository.ts:33-36). A lost S24 race would therefore leave an orphan account.
gaps.proposedFix: Change the DTO to terms: TermsAcceptanceClaimDto[] and validate it with assertClaimsArePublished. Name the AcceptanceMethod value for Ever ID sign-up. Say how the create-account page gets the required documents. Replace 'one transaction' with an explicit order: take the (issuer, subject) link or a pre-check under the unique index before creating the user, or compensate by deleting the just-created user when insertLink fails. Record terms best-effort as register does, and update the T15 assertions.

gaps.title: T20 API integration spec cannot load the ESM-only identity libraries under apps/api Jest
gaps.evidence: T20 (tasks.md:252-262, plan.md:761) runs the real controller, services and guard with the T8 fake provider under apps/api Jest. apps/api/jest.config.js uses a ts-jest CommonJS transform with no ESM handling and no moduleNameMapper entry for @ever-works/oidc-identity or its /testing subpath. openid-client@6.8.4 and jose@6.2.3 (node_modules/.pnpm) are both 'type: module' with a default-only export. Production loads plugins by import() (packages/agent/src/plugins/services/plugin-loader.service.ts:339), but Jest's CommonJS runtime cannot require them. The spec never says whether the facade gets a real plugin instance or a stub.
gaps.proposedFix: State the harness. Either bind IdentityProviderFacadeService to an in-test IIdentityProviderPlugin that uses only node:crypto (the fake provider source, mapped by path in jest.config.js), or move the flow spec to a Vitest lane that loads the real plugin. Add the jest.config.js moduleNameMapper change to T20's file list.

gaps.title: Playwright connect specs need to change session and account rows that the e2e lane cannot reach
gaps.evidence: T30 (tasks.md:352-353) and plan.md:775 require 'connect with a session aged past 12 h in the database → S15' and an S14 account (no password, no social provider, unverified e-mail; spec.md:138-140). gaps.title: No task builds the administrator surface (S10, spec §6.7) or logs FR-4 configuration changes

gaps.title: Fake GitHub route and fault list omits APIs the PR-lane scenarios and other epics call

gaps.title: The managed tier refuses crons more frequent than every 5 minutes, yet the fixture (every 2 min) and Cal.diy (every minute) are the Blueprints meant to run there
gaps.evidence: APW-06 plan §4.9 (L424) says schedules firing more often than every 5 minutes are refused on `ever-works-apps` (`cron_too_frequent`, constant L570). The zone CRD also requires `schedule (≥ 5 min)` (APW-10 plan L245). The fixture's `tick` is `*/2 * * * *` (works.yml L106-110), and Cal.diy's `tasker` and `webhook-triggers` are `* * * * *` (L198-202, L228-232). APW-13 verification (FR-32/33) runs on a Your-cluster test cluster only, so a Blueprint can become 'Verified', and thus eligible for managed hosting, while the tier would refuse it. ACC-E2E-10 (b) uses the fixture on the managed tier.
gaps.proposedFix: Give each Blueprint a managed-tier-compatible profile (a crons ≥ 5 min variant for the fixture; a documented decision for Cal.diy's minute-level task queue). Add to APW-03 a Blueprint-mode check that labels an entry `managedHosting: entryDisallows` when its crons violate the tier minimum. Make APW-13 verification include a managed-constraint lint.

gaps.title: ACC-E2E-10(b) cannot obtain an App Work 'resolved from a verified Blueprint'

Alternatively use a long-lived Link repository listed in the entry for E2E-10 (b). Update ACCEPTANCE preconditions.

gaps.title: Ten fixture variant branches and five App spec profiles are not drafted
