gaps.title: The Umami and Cal.diy Blueprint drafts use reserved EVER_WORKS_* env names and would fail App spec validation
gaps.evidence: I ran a validator (yaml@2.8.3 from the worktree's node_modules) implementing schema.md §12, §21 and §22 rules over the three drafts. app-fixture-hello passes. umami/.works/works.yml:76-77 declares EVER_WORKS_WEB_INTERNAL_URL and EVER_WORKS_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD. cal-diy/.works/works.yml:119, 134 and 137 declare EVER_WORKS_WEB_INTERNAL_URL, EVER_WORKS_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_EMAIL and EVER_WORKS_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD, which the inline bootstrap job scripts also read (umami :95, :107; cal-diy :179-186). gaps.title: The kind e2e lane never allow-lists the loopback cluster API, so APW-06 refuses every deploy there

The nightly and golden-path lanes are exposed the same way whenever the test cluster API is not public.

gaps.title: Fixture Dockerfile design has no numeric USER; the fixture would be refused under the platform's default security context
gaps.evidence: plan.md §4.1 describes the fixture Dockerfile as 'node:22-alpine; stage `runtime`; ARG FIXTURE_BUILD_LABEL → ENV', with no USER. Official node images run as root by default and ship user `node` with uid 1000. app-fixture-hello works.yml sets `writableRootFilesystem: false` and expects to deploy in under a minute. APW-06 plan §4.4 renders `runAsNonRoot: true` with no runAsUser, which leads to kubelet 'image will run as root' and `image_runs_as_root`. A `USER node` (a name) would instead fail as `image_user_unverifiable` (kubelet security_context_others.go L50). ACC-13-01/02/03 and every fixture variant depend on the pod starting.
gaps.proposedFix:
1) plan §4.1 Dockerfile line becomes: 'node:22-alpine; stage `runtime`; `USER 1000` (numeric: the image's `node` user); ARG FIXTURE_BUILD_LABEL → ENV'.
2) blueprints/app-fixture-hello/README.md feature table: add the row 'Non-root image | the pod starts under the platform's default security context (numeric USER)'.
3) The /data volume stays writable through APW-06's fsGroup (plan §4.4), so no other change is needed.

gaps.title: Cal.diy build DATABASE_URL is a literal URL for a user and database the build service never creates; the 'trust authentication' TODO is wrong
gaps.evidence:
cal-diy works.yml L60-L70 pass the literal `postgresql://postgres@localhost:5432/calendso`, with TODO(verify, APW-05) on the host and on 'trust authentication'. What APW-05 and APW-07 actually do:
- APW-05 plan §4.4 (L170-L199): services run as workflow `services` with ports, and buildx uses `network: host`.
- APW-05 plan §4.7 (L704): build values resolve 'against build.services (e.g. postgresql://ever-works-build:ever-works-build@127.0.0.1:5432/app, flagged fromBuildService)'.
- APW-07 plan §4.6.2 (L421-L432): postgres build-service outputs are `url` = `directUrl` = `postgresql://user:password@127.0.0.1:5432/database?sslmode=disable`, with injected defaults ever-works-build / ever-works-build / app.
- APW-05 spec FR-20: a dependency-output reference of the same name resolves to the build service.
- APW-03 schema §21: `fromEnv` needs an env entry with phase build|both.
Upstream side: the Dockerfile declares only `ARG DATABASE_URL` (L10) and copies it into DATABASE_DIRECT_URL for the build (L21-L30). Upstream's own image test builds against a password-authenticated database on localhost:5432: https://github.com/calcom/cal.diy/blob/6bc45298226f96ff79e0c070c8b2ce39727e8477/.github/actions/docker-build-and-test/action.yml#L70-L117
gaps.proposedFix:
1) cal-diy works.yml build args: replace the literal with `- { name: DATABASE_URL, fromEnv: DATABASE_URL }`.
2) Change the env entry to `- { name: DATABASE_URL, secret: true, phase: both, from: deps.postgres.url }`. At build it resolves to the throwaway service; at run time, to the App dependency.
3) Keep `services: [{ name: postgres, image: 'postgres:16' }]`.
4) Delete both `TODO(verify, APW-05)` comments and the trust-authentication comment.
5) README 'Unverified' item 2 becomes 'Resolved: build services are reached on 127.0.0.1 with throwaway credentials (APW-05 plan §4.7, APW-07 plan §4.6.2)'.
6) plan §7.1 row 'Ephemeral postgres:16 during the build, DATABASE_URL build arg' becomes '… DATABASE_URL passed with fromEnv and resolved to the build service'.

gaps.title: Cal.diy administrator password check uses look-ahead, which the App spec's RE2 rule rejects
gaps.evidence: cal-diy works.yml L144: `validate: { pattern: "^(?=.*[a-z])(?=.*[A-Z])(?=.*\\d).{15,}$" }`. APW-03 schema.md §12: `validate.pattern` uses 'RE2 syntax (no back-references or look-around: `pattern_unsupported`)'. The Blueprint repository's validate.yml (T28 done-when) therefore fails. The upstream rule, confirmed at the pin: apps/web/app/api/auth/setup/route.ts L23-L27 calls `isPasswordValid(val.trim(), false, true)`. packages/lib/auth/isPasswordValid.ts in strict mode requires length > 14, a digit, a lower-case and an upper-case letter, all checked on the TRIMMED value: https://github.com/calcom/cal.diy/blob/6bc45298226f96ff79e0c070c8b2ce39727e8477/packages/lib/auth/isPasswordValid.ts
gaps.proposedFix:
1) Replace the entry with `validate: { minLength: 15, pattern: '^(?:.*[a-z].*[A-Z].*[0-9].*|.*[a-z].*[0-9].*[A-Z].*|.*[A-Z].*[a-z].*[0-9].*|.*[A-Z].*[0-9].*[a-z].*|.*[0-9].*[a-z].*[A-Z].*|.*[0-9].*[A-Z].*[a-z].*)$' }`. RE2 accepts this.
2) Append 'no leading or trailing spaces' to the prompt description, because the setup route checks the trimmed value.
3) Point the `# verified` comment at apps/web/app/api/auth/setup/route.ts and packages/lib/auth/isPasswordValid.ts.

gaps.title: No draft exists for the license registry, the bundled snapshot or the catalog manifest entries

gaps.title: No program-level threat model for running and evolving untrusted repositories
gaps.proposedFix:
Create docs/specs/features/app-works/THREAT-MODEL.md, following public-repository hygiene: generic wording, no addresses, no unfixed findings. Outline:
1. Assets: user code, forks, App env secrets, Git and registry tokens, kubeconfigs, tenant data, platform credentials, user reputation upstream.
2. Actors: malicious upstream author, malicious or compromised App Work owner (tenant), co-tenant, compromised catalog contributor, abusive contributor, external attacker against user-app domains.
3. Trust-boundary table covering the boundaries listed in the evidence.
4. For each boundary, STRIDE threats → control (FR / LG / R-n / rule) → verifying test (ACC-NEG/ACC-xx) → residual risk and the wave in which it is accepted.
5. Items deliberately kept in the private operations repository (pointer only).
6. Posture change: agents reading untrusted repositories must run in an enforcing sandbox or on a Fleet node (APW-04/08).
Append matching rows to docs/specs/security/THREAT-MODEL.md §2 and its §8 revision log, and link the new file from README companion documents and each plan's constitution checklist.

gaps.title: The upstream sync pull request can run workflows newly added upstream, because hygiene runs only after the merge
gaps.evidence: APW-02 FR-25 and FR-28 (spec L293-299): hygiene disables workflows present at readiness, then again 'after every upstream sync that changed the tracked branch and after a sync pull request is merged'. FR-36 (L315-317) pushes upstream's head to `ever-works/upstream-sync` in the fork and opens a same-repository PR. Workflow files added upstream since the last hygiene run are not disabled while that branch push and PR exist, so their push or pull_request triggers run on the fork (for Cal.diy, on every sync that adds a workflow). This breaks the ACC-E2E-02 guarantee of no inherited workflow runs and spends the user's Actions minutes.
gaps.proposedFix: Before pushing `ever-works/upstream-sync`, diff `.github/workflows/**` between the tracked branch and upstream's head. Either strip new workflow files from the sync branch (keeping them in a follow-up list for review), or disable them by path right after the push and before opening the PR. Add an ACC-NEG case covering an upstream commit that adds a workflow.

A stale branch left after a merged PR takes the same path. 4. If a PR is open, update its title and body to the new version. Otherwise run `createPullRequest`. 5. gaps.title: POST /provision semantics contradict S21 and S10
gaps.evidence: The error table (plan.md:466-467) says an active provisioning without restart → 409 provisioningActive, yet a 'duplicate start within the partial-unique window' → 202 deduplicated, and the window is never defined. S21 (spec.md:165-166) says two Re-provision clicks yield one provisioning, but Re-provision sends restart:true, which cancels and starts again, so a double click makes two. Readiness false → 422 with no row (plan.md:465), and S10 says no Task exists, yet failure reason 'no-isolated-runtime' (spec.md:423) implies a failed row. What start({trigger:'auto-create'}) does when readiness is false is unspecified.
gaps.proposedFix: Define the dedupe rule (for example, the same user with restart:true within 10 s returns the newest row with deduplicated:true), whether 409 or 202 is returned for a non-restart start while active, and whether an auto-create start with readiness false writes a failed/no-isolated-runtime row or nothing.

reasons: c: real, important — I checked the current files and the gap is real. Two points in the auditor's evidence are slightly overstated. 1) The two rows in the error table overlap (APW-04 plan.md:466-467). The only partial-unique index is `uq_work_app_provisionings_active` (plan §3.1): UNIQUE (workId) WHERE status IN ('queued','running','needs_input'). So the "partial-unique window" can only mean "while an active row exists", which is exactly when the 409 row applies. Nothing in the plan, tasks, CONTRACTS §4, ACCEPTANCE
verify.refinedFix: A. APW-04 plan.md §3.2 `APP_PROVISION_LIMITS`: add `startDedupeMs: 10_000`. Extend the T6 contracts pin test in tasks.md to cover it. B. APW-04 plan.md §4: replace the rows "Active provisioning and restart !== true" and "Duplicate start within the partial-unique window". Add a subsection "Start semantics" that `AppProvisioningService.start({ workId, userId, trigger, restart?, note? })` evaluates in this order, in one transaction on the Work's active row: 1. Not kind app → 422 notAppWork. 2. Dedupe: an active row (queued|running|needs_input) for the Work created ≤ `startDedupeMs` ago → 202 `{ provisioningId: <that row>, status, deduplicated: true }`. This applies whatever `restart`, trigger or caller; nothing is cancelled and no row is written. 3. Active row older than the window and `restart !== true`: - manual/chat → 409 `{ code: 'provisioningActive', provisioningId, status }`; - `auto-create`, `upstream-smoke` and `auto-upstream-smoke` → return the active row as a no-op (never 409, never cancel). 4. Readiness has any false flag: - manual/chat → 422 provisioningUnavailable `{ missing }`; - automatic triggers → return `{ started: false, missing }` without throwing. In both cases: no row, no Task, no Run, no `app.provision.started`, and nothing is cancelled even when `restart` is true. The card derives "No isolated sandbox" from `GET …/provisioning` readiness. There is no automatic retry; once readiness is true the card shows Not started → Provision. 5. `restart === true` with an active row older than the window: only manual/chat may pass it. In the same transaction, compare-and-set the old row to cancelled (its Run, Build and verification target are cancelled via the `cancel` event after commit), insert the new row, return 202 deduplicated:false. 6. No active row → insert (queued with `queuedReason` when the 3-per-user or 10-per-org cap is reached) → 202 deduplicated:false. 7. An insert that loses `uq_work_app_provisionings_active` (concurrent start) → re-read the active row → 202 `{ provisioningId, status, deduplicated: true }`, never 409 or 500. Also in plan §5, on AppReprovisionDialog: send `restart: true` only in the running-provisioning variant, and reopen that variant on a 409. The chat tool `provisionAppWork` never sends `restart`. C. APW-04 plan.md, `no-isolated-runtime` scope: - §6.3 sweeper item 5: re-check readiness before promoting a queued row; if `isolatedRuntime` is false → failed/no-isolated-runtime. - §10.2: add a row "Isolated runtime lost after the row exists (queued promotion or before a run dispatch) → failed/no-isolated-runtime, no Run dispatched". - §11.1 service spec: extend with the dedupe window (restart and non-restart), the 409 outside the window, a lost unique insert returning the winner, 422 with restart:true cancelling nothing, auto-create with readiness false writing nothing and not throwing, and queued promotion with isolatedRuntime false failing with that reason. D. APW-04 spec.md: - S21: reword to "Two starts of the same App Work within 10 seconds — two Provision or Re-provision confirmations, including two 'Cancel it and start over?' confirmations — create exactly one provisioning; the second returns the first one's id and cancels nothing." - FR-44: add "a start within 10 seconds of the active provisioning's start returns it". - §5.3: add a sentence that `no-isolated-runtime` applies only to a provisioning that already exists and loses its isolated sandbox before a run starts; a start refused for readiness creates no provisioning (S10). E. APW-04 tasks.md: - T19 test: add the cases from C. - T23 test: 409 only outside the 10 s window; a double restart inside the window yields one id with deduplicated:true (ACC-04-03). - T24: auto-create with readiness false returns `{ started: false }`, writes no row and does not throw; test it in `app-provisioning.auto-start.spec.ts`. - T25: dialog sends `restart` only in the running variant. ACCEPTANCE.md ACC-04-03 row: optionally append "including two restart confirmations within 10 s".

gaps.title: One Provisioner Agent per Organization conflicts with the run ownership check

There is one per person in their personal space and one per person in each Organization. It is created on first use and reused for that person's later provisionings in that scope. Agents are never shared between Organization members: each member who provisions gets their own." Add to FR-8: "The Task is owned by the same person and scope as the Agent." Add acceptance criterion ACC-04-39: "Two editors of App Works in one Organization each provision. Each run is assigned to and executed by the starter's own App Provisioner Agent, and no run ends agent-not-found. APW-06's precondition `env_required_unset` reads `unsetRequired: string[]` (APW-06 plan.md:492, 911), with no descriptions and no copy or i18n in APW-06.
gaps.proposedFix: Add a CONTRACTS row: APW-06's Deploy tab renders APW-07's `DeployBlockedByEnvNotice` for `env_required_unset`. The precondition carries `names[]` plus descriptions (from `AppEnvService.missingRequired`, or add `unsetRequired: {name, description}[]` to the port). Add the APW-06 task and test.

gaps.title: No state for external providers waiting on the owner's settings, and no defined meaning for an optional SMTP
gaps.evidence: FR-36 makes 'Your own SMTP server' (prompted host, password, …) the default SMTP provider. reconcile inserts `pending` and dispatches at once (plan.md:139-146), and the SMTP readiness deadline is 30 s (plan.md:284), so the card reaches `failed deadlineExceeded` before the owner can configure anything. The status enum (plan.md:187) and spec §6.3 have no 'needs configuration' state or copy. APW-03 schema.md:215 makes `smtp.required` default `false`, yet an env entry `from: deps.smtp.*` becomes unresolved `dependencyNotReady` and blocks Deploy (FR-23/26), so 'optional' SMTP still blocks.
gaps.proposedFix: Add status `awaiting_config` (card copy 'Needs your settings', i18n key, no dispatch until PUT config, no deadline). Define that when `smtp.required: false` and SMTP isn't configured, referencing entries are left out (or resolve empty) rather than blocking, and state what `required: true` blocks. Add T16/T17/T25 test cases.

gaps.title: Owner decision needed: which S3-compatible server runs in the user's cluster (blocks T19 images and T21)
gaps.evidence: spec.md:618-620 leaves [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: which S3-compatible server in the cluster] open. P1 T19 needs a digest-pinned image in `images.ts` (tasks.md:249-250). T21 and plan.md:543 assume one product's admin model: provider id `k8s-inline-minio`, a root user, and an init Job that creates a service account whose keys go to `dep-s3-app`. A different server changes the init Job, the outputs and the tests.
gaps.proposedFix: Owner picks the default in-cluster S3-compatible server (and whether the provider id stays product-named). The plan then fixes the init Job commands, secret keys and image digest to match.

gaps.title: The value-free runner recipe for verification builds has no fixed format, and dependency host names disagree with APW-05
gaps.evidence: APW-07 plan.md:415 defines recipe entries with tokens `{{gen:NAME}}`, `{{prompted:NAME}}`, `{{gen:DEP_<KIND>_PASSWORD}}` and 'APW-05's runner container names'. The type in APW-06 plan.md:930-935 and CONTRACTS.md:283 is `spec: unknown`. APW-05 plan.md:776-782 names the throwaway containers `postgres`, `redis`, `minio` and defines no `DEP_*` token or how container credentials are set. APW-07's build-service mapping uses `object-storage` (plan.md:422). T43 only checks that the recipe holds no value (tasks.md:531), so the two epics can each build a different format.
gaps.proposedFix: Add a normative `AppEnvRecipeEntry` discriminated union in `packages/contracts/src/apps/app-env.ts`: token grammar, per-kind runner host names, ports, user/db names and credential tokens, and the keypair/alphabet parameters. Reference it from CONTRACTS §3 and APW-05 §4.10. Add a shape test in T43 and in APW-05's plan-schema test.

gaps.title: The in-zone dependency contract APW-07 requested from APW-10 has no implementing task (P2)
gaps.evidence: The CONTRACTS.md:300 row (owner APW-10) covers `Work.status.dependencies[] { kind, ref, phase, lastBackupAt }`, in-zone substitution of `ew-dep://<kind>/<output>` rejecting unknown tokens, and tenant Postgres DDL from `tenant-postgres-ddl.ts`. `grep -n 'ew-dep://'` in APW-10 plan/tasks returns nothing. APW-10 tasks mention `status.dependencies` only for removal (APW-10 tasks.md:90, 596). No task provisions tenant Postgres, per-App-Work Redis or bucket users, or records backups at least daily (FR-50). APW-07 T36/T37 and ACC-07-26…28 depend on it.
gaps.proposedFix: Add APW-10 P2 tasks for the controller: provision dependencies from `Work.spec.dependencies` using `buildTenantPostgresDdl`, per-App-Work Redis, prefixed buckets with quota, token substitution with unknown-token refusal, a backup schedule ≤ 24 h writing `lastBackupAt`, and tests. Also confirm the `IAppsTierProvider.applyWork` input shape that T36 writes.

gaps.title: T40's parity test can't import APW-03's schema from the contracts package, and APW-03 builds its own copy of the outputs list
gaps.evidence: T40 creates `packages/contracts/src/apps/__tests__/dependency-outputs-parity.spec.ts` to compare against the schema in `packages/agent/src/works-config/schema/` (tasks.md:486-488). `@ever-works/contracts` has zero dependencies (packages/contracts/package.json) and must not import the agent package. APW-03 T4 (APW-03 tasks.md:86-87) creates its own 'output tables per dependency' in `app-spec.refs.ts`, although CONTRACTS.md:259 makes APW-07 the owner of `APP_DEPENDENCY_OUTPUTS`. The keypair-format enum parity has the same problem.
gaps.proposedFix: Make APW-03's reference resolver and JSON Schema import `APP_DEPENDENCY_OUTPUTS` and `APP_ENV_KEYPAIR_FORMATS` from `@ever-works/contracts` (APW-07 T1/T2 land first, or APW-03 creates them with APW-07's exact values). Move T40's parity spec to `packages/agent/src/works-config/schema/__tests__/` and name that command.

gaps.title: FR-37 volume size editing (grow allowed, shrink refused) has no task, error code or test
gaps.evidence: spec.md:309-310 says default sizes are 'editable per App Work before first provisioning; growing later is allowed, shrinking is refused'. The PUT body carries `sizeGiB` (plan.md:642), but T19/T20/T21/T25 implement no volume-claim expansion. The error list (plan.md:652-655) has no shrink-refusal code, and there is no reason for a storage class that can't expand. Provider settings require `appDependencySizes` '≥ defaults' (plan.md:556), which conflicts with per-App-Work editing below the default.
gaps.proposedFix: Add a task: PUT validates `sizeGiB` (minimum, no shrink → 422 `sizeShrinkRefused`), a `resize` provision mode patches the volume claim when the storage class allows expansion (otherwise reason `volumeExpansionUnsupported`), with k8s provider and controller tests. Reconcile the settings rule with FR-37.

gaps.title: Managed App dependencies and their backups are not clearly metered
gaps.evidence: The APW-10 plan §3.2 UsageReport carries `cpuCoreSeconds, memoryMiBHours, egressMiB, storageGiBHours, buildMinutes` per App Work. The P2 providers `managed-postgres`, `managed-redis` and `managed-object-storage` (CONTRACTS §3) run on shared tenant data servers (D8), whose per-App-Work storage, connections and backup storage fall outside any namespace meter. APW-07 spec and tasks contain no meter or receipt, which conflicts with README §7 rule 12.
gaps.proposedFix: APW-07 P2 and APW-10: add units for dependency storage and backup GiB-hours and an import path (the `Work.status.dependencies[]` usage), priced on the credit list and included in the daily receipt, with an ACC.

gaps.title: The platform mail relay lets untrusted code on Your cluster send mail with no eligibility, account cap, abuse signal or metering
gaps.evidence: APW-07 FR-39 (spec lines 313-315) offers the 'Ever Works mail relay' from Wave 1 with only 200 messages per App Work per day, sending from the relay's no-reply domain. Nothing checks for a verified or paying account, caps per account (the limit multiplies by the uncapped App Work count, see XC-11), or raises abuse signals (APW-10 Mail signals exist only on the tier). No receipt is produced either (rule 12).
gaps.proposedFix: Limit the relay to verified accounts, add per-account and per-organization daily caps, bounce/complaint suspension and a kill switch (XC-10), meter it with a receipt, and add ACCs.

gaps.title: T22 as written cannot compile: the PR-status sweep never has the provider status, base ref or merge commit sha
gaps.evidence: T22 (tasks.md:355-361) calls `TaskDeliveryService.isDeliveryTracked(after, status)` inside `syncDuePrStatuses`. That loop holds only the Task returned by `refreshTask` (task-pr-status.service.ts:272-283). `refreshTask` reads `GitPullRequestStatus` internally and writes a cache patch, not the status (task-pr-status.service.ts:376-395). `Task` stores no baseRef or mergeCommitSha (task.entity.ts; plan.md:38).
gaps.proposedFix: Specify in T22/plan §2.4 how the status reaches the hook: refreshTask returns `{ task, status }`, or the cache patch persists `mergeCommitSha` and the base ref. List the refactor and keep existing sweep tests unchanged.

gaps.title: Isolated-run admission needs Fleet placement at dispatch time, but dispatchAgentRun does not know where a run will go
gaps.evidence: T12 (tasks.md:212-216) defines `isAppWorkRunAdmitted(task, plan)`, which admits 'when the run is planned for a Fleet node', and says the refusal lives in `dispatchAgentRun`. In `dispatchAgentRun`, placement is decided later inside `dispatcher.enqueue`, by a routing adapter reading the tenant job runtime config (task-transition.service.ts:1063-1076). No `plan` object exists, and no task names the type, where it comes from, or how a Fleet router that falls back to cloud is treated.
gaps.proposedFix: Name the placement source (e.g. the tenant job-runtime selector / fleet routing adapter), the `plan` type and the refusal site. Alternatively, move the check into the routing adapter and the cloud worker (refuse before provisioning) and add those files to T12.

gaps.title: Keyed Task-thread posts ({ key, params }) have no storage, migration or renderer
gaps.evidence: plan.md:596 says stored system posts carry a key and params, rendered in the reader's locale. T26 (tasks.md:406-408) posts `{ key, params }` through postSystemMessage/TaskChatService. But task_chat_messages has only `body text` and a NOT NULL uuid `authorId` (task-chat-message.entity.ts:44-51). `postSystemMessage(input, body: string)` posts `authorType 'agent'` with `authorId = agentId` (task-workspace.service.ts:2340-2352). No task adds a column, migration, DTO or web renderer. Reconciler posts on Tasks with no Agent (R-21 null agentId) would have no authorId.
gaps.proposedFix: Either post pre-rendered English like the existing system posts and drop the plan §5.2 claim, or add a task: new nullable `messageKey`/`messageParams` columns plus a migration in block 179208, author fallback for unassigned Tasks, and the web chat renderer with tests.

gaps.title: Mission template: wrong catalog layout, wrong entry form, and no way to fetch the manifest
gaps.evidence: T41 (tasks.md:591-599) and CONTRACTS.md:427 put the template in a folder of `ever-works/missions`. The seed mechanism is one repository per template (`MissionTemplateConfig{owner, repo, branch}`, packages/agent/src/missions/mission-template.config.ts:27-60), and no code reads `ever-works/missions`. The draft itself leaves this open (mission-template-draft/.works/mission.yml:3-5). 'Use this Template' links to `/new?type=mission&template=<id>`, handled by NewPageClient (apps/web/src/components/templates/TemplatesCatalog.tsx:376-390; apps/web/src/components/new/NewPageClient.tsx:355-371), but T40 changes `NewMissionForm.tsx` (`/missions/new`). T38 says 'fetch and apply the manifest', yet MissionTemplateManifestService is a pure parser with no fetcher (mission-template-manifest.service.ts:17-22), and no API returns a manifest's `appWork` to the web.
gaps.proposedFix: Choose the repository `ever-works/build-on-open-source-app-mission-template` and update CONTRACTS §8 and the draft header. Name the manifest fetch (git facade read of `.works/mission.yml` at the template branch) and a read endpoint for the web. Retarget T40/T42 to NewPageClient, or change the template card link.

gaps.title: P1 binds the evolve-app Skill before P3 publishes it, and binding is neither installed first nor idempotent
gaps.evidence: T25 (P1, tasks.md:388-391) binds `evolve-app` through `SkillsService.createBinding` 'idempotent on the unique index'. createBinding first calls `getOne(userId, skillId)`, so the user must already own an installed Skill row (skills.service.ts:281-288; installFromCatalog at :234). It then inserts into unique `uq_skill_binding` (skill-binding.entity.ts:33), which throws on a duplicate rather than being a no-op. The Skill reaches `ever-works/skills` only in P3 T41 (tasks.md:591-594). The catalog's manifest.json row (slug, skillPath, name, summary, tags, version, license, sourceUrl — docs/features/skills-catalog.md:75-78) has no draft next to skill-draft/SKILL.md.
gaps.proposedFix: Move Skill publication (T41's skills half) before T25, or make T25 skip binding when the catalog Skill is absent. Specify `installFromCatalog` then binding, with a find-first check. Add a draft manifest.json row next to skill-draft/SKILL.md.

gaps.title: FR-53 per-run budget for Mission-filed Tasks has no mechanism
gaps.evidence: T35 (tasks.md:523-524) dispatches 'with the run budget from guardrailsOverride.maxBudgetCentsPerRun'. `dispatchAgentRun` accepts only generation, dedupKey, delegationScope, seedPendingInput and reviewId (task-transition.service.ts:853-915). No per-run cost cap exists for cloud agent runs: `maxBudgetCentsPerRun` is read only by the Idea/Work agent (work-agent.service.ts:360), and Fleet has only agent-settings `maxBudgetUsd` (fleet-agent-task-planner.service.ts:274, 328). The template promises '$15.00 per run' (spec FR-57, S12).
gaps.proposedFix: Add a dispatch option (e.g. `maxBudgetCents`) stored on the run and enforced by the cloud worker, and mapped to `execution.maxBudgetUsd` on Fleet. Add the files and tests to T35, or declare FR-53 out of scope and change the FR-57 copy.

gaps.title: Telemetry task makes the agent package import @ever-works/monitoring, which it does not depend on
gaps.evidence: T43 (tasks.md:610-619) has agent-package services (app-change-request.service.ts, app-change-guard.ts, task-delivery.service.ts, mission-tick.service.ts) call `emitAppChangeEvent` from packages/monitoring. packages/agent/package.json has no @ever-works/monitoring dependency. Existing agent telemetry avoids that dependency on purpose, through an injected capture-client interface (packages/agent/src/services/knowledge-base-reconcile.service.ts:55-66). `emitKbEvent`, the model T43 copies, has no production caller.
gaps.proposedFix: Specify a DI token plus capture-client interface in the agent package (as KB reconcile does), bound by apps/api to PostHog. Keep the typed event and forbidden-key guard in monitoring, called at the binding.

gaps.title: Delivery SQL and the 'merge recorded once' index work only on Postgres/SQLite; MySQL and MariaDB are supported
gaps.evidence: plan.md:612-614 uses `"deliveryState" IS NOT DISTINCT FROM :from` for compare-and-set. plan.md:328-330 and 435-438 rely on a partial unique index and branch only on Postgres vs SQLite. `DATABASE_TYPE` 'mysql' is wired in packages/agent/src/database/database-config.factory.ts:142-150. Commit b5a7d6857, which landed after the program was verified, fixed exactly this class of Postgres/SQLite-only SQL for mysql/mariadb in the activity feed repository. MySQL has neither partial indexes nor IS NOT DISTINCT FROM, so S29's 'database guarantee' does not hold there.
gaps.proposedFix: In plan §3.5/§6, add a driver branch: MySQL `<=>` (or a portable `(col = :from OR (col IS NULL AND :from IS NULL))`), and an application-level uniqueness check with a lock when partial indexes are unavailable. Add mysql cases to the T9 migration spec and T21.

gaps.title: APP_WORK_AGENT_RESOLVER is registered in a module APW-02 never imports, so conflict Tasks would silently get no Agent
gaps.evidence: APW-08 registers AppWorkRulesService, the guard, delivery services and the resolver in TasksDomainModule (`packages/agent/src/tasks-domain/tasks.module.ts`; tasks.md:177-179, 392-394). APW-02 creates `packages/agent/src/app-works/app-works.module.ts` (APW-02 tasks.md:231) and injects `APP_WORK_AGENT_RESOLVER` as `@Optional()` into AppUpstreamStateService (APW-02 tasks.md:317-319). No task provides `{ provide: APP_WORK_AGENT_RESOLVER, useExisting: AppWorkAgentResolver }` in a module that AppWorksModule can see. An unbound @Optional token resolves to undefined, so APW-02's null-agent branch runs silently (ACC-08-32 / ACC-02-11).
gaps.proposedFix: In T25, bind the token explicitly and state which module exports it and which module imports it (e.g. provide it in AppWorksModule, or have AppWorksModule import TasksDomainModule if that creates no cycle). Add a module-compilation test proving the injection is defined.

gaps.title: No task implements FR-14 (owner asked once to review checks) or FR-61 (missing tool, not re-offered to the same node)
gaps.evidence: FR-14 (spec.md:243-246) asks the owner once when an App spec is first applied and whenever its checks change. FR-61 (spec.md:398-400) reports 'Error — a tool this check needs is missing on this machine' and excludes that node for the Task. Only the i18n key `appRules.missingTool` exists (plan.md:577). T13 and T14 cover admission and a settings card only, and grepping tasks.md for FR-14/FR-61, 're-offer' or a notification finds nothing. The node runs checks with `shell: true` (apps/node/src/core/executors/acceptance-checks.ts:~363), so a missing tool shows as a red exit code, not `error`, and no detection rule is given.
gaps.proposedFix: Add a task that notifies the owner (Inbox or notification) from the app.spec.applied listener when `checks` changes, deduplicated per spec hash. Add a Fleet task: classify exit 127 (POSIX) and 9009 (Windows) as missing tool, record the node id on the Task/run, and exclude it in the fleet dispatcher. Include tests.

gaps.title: request_app_change chat tool gets no keyword slot, so tool selection can leave it out of every turn
gaps.evidence: registry-parity.unit.spec.ts:5-16 records that 'a registry entry with no keyword slot is gated out of every turn, which is how the Mission-create outage happened'. tool-selection.ts:62-145 requires keyword slots under a 'program DoD rule', and generated tools may never be always-on (tool-selection.ts:350-360). T26 (tasks.md:402-412) only appends the registry row and runs registry-parity. It adds no DOMAIN_KEYWORDS slot and no `selectActiveToolNames` test for phrasings like 'add an SMS reminder to my app'.
gaps.proposedFix: Extend T26: modify apps/web/src/lib/ai/tools/tool-selection.ts with a slot (or STATIC_TOOL_DOMAINS entry) for request_app_change, and add parity cases showing representative change requests reach the tool and unrelated turns do not.

gaps.title: Some user-visible copy and actions have no i18n keys or API contract (spec-invalid, diff-unreadable, S22 Inbox item, S28, FR-54, Try once more)
gaps.evidence: These strings have no key in plan §5.2 (plan.md:524-596): the plan.md:670-671 refusals ('The App spec on {branch} is invalid…', 'Couldn't verify this change's files. Try again.'); the S22 Inbox item and its actions Open the Task / Close anyway / Try once more (spec.md:168-170); and the S28 push-credential copy (spec.md:183-185). FR-54's once-a-day Activity entry names no actionType/action in CONTRACTS §6. 'Try once more' is `202` in CONTRACTS.md:323 but '200 allowed once per Inbox item' in plan.md:468, and `POST /api/tasks/:id/delivery/follow-up` takes no body identifying the escalation/Inbox item, so 'once per item' cannot be enforced as written.
gaps.proposedFix: Add the missing keys to plan §5.2 and T28. Define the S22 Inbox item as a `delivery-failed` escalation with action ids. Give the follow-up endpoint a body `{ escalationId }` with one-shot consumption and a single status code, and align CONTRACTS §4. Name the FR-54 Activity action (e.g. `mission.task_output.nothing_to_file`).

gaps.title: APW-08 limits disagree with the APW-03 schema: check timeouts, instruction files, maxPullRequestChangedFiles
gaps.evidence: APW-03 schema.md §17 (lines 363-368) sets `checks[].timeoutSeconds` default 1800, range 60–7200. APW-08 FR-18 (spec.md:257) and plan.md:197-198 use 1–3600, default 600. The golden Blueprints use 3600 (APW-13-golden-paths/blueprints/cal-diy/.works/works.yml:262-275), and APW-05 maps ceil(timeoutSeconds/60) minutes. Schema §18 (lines 372-376) allows `instructionFiles` ≤ 10, while FR-23 and `APP_INSTRUCTION_FILES_MAX = 5` (plan.md:389) cap at 5. The schema also defines `maxPullRequestChangedFiles` (default 50, 1–500), which no epic enforces, while FR-21 uses 300 files.
gaps.proposedFix: Pick one set of bounds and apply it in APW-03 schema.md and APW-08 spec/plan constants: adopt the schema's timeout range, state what happens to instruction files beyond 5 (warning issue code or schema cap of 5), and either enforce `maxPullRequestChangedFiles` in AppChangeGuard or remove it from the schema.

gaps.title: Provisioner exemption and follow-up dedup rely on user-editable Task labels; the dedup label is also longer than the 80-character cap
gaps.evidence: T17 exempts Tasks labelled `app-provision` from App spec field protection (tasks.md:287-291). T21 and plan.md:606 deduplicate follow-ups with the label `followup:<taskId>:<failureId>`. Labels can be set through create/update Task by users and by the `create_task`/`update_task` chat tools (packages/agent/src/tasks-domain/tasks.service.ts:114-118; apps/web/src/lib/ai/tools/generated/registry.ts:385-395). Any Task can therefore opt out of source/license/blueprint protection, and dedup can be bypassed. Two UUIDs plus the prefix make 82 characters, over `@MaxLength(80, { each: true })` (apps/api/src/tasks/tasks.dto.ts:62-72), so a later label update on that Task fails validation. APW-04 also uses its own finalize variants (APW-04 tasks.md:222-226), so the finalizeRun exemption never applies to it.
gaps.proposedFix: Key the exemption on `WorkAppProvisioning.taskId` (APW-04 entity), not a label. Store follow-up lineage as a `follow-up` relation plus a server-side dedup key (a column, or an escalation dedupKey), or shorten the label to fit 80 characters. Add tests that a user-added label grants nothing.

gaps.title: No Agent exists to evolve a Blueprint-created App Work: the chat asks the user to pick from zero Agents
gaps.evidence: APW-08 FR-42 (spec L348-351) resolves the change Agent from a recent Task, the only pinned Agent or the only assigned Agent, else asks (S25: 'offering Maya's Agents'). The resolver returns null otherwise (plan L294-302). A Blueprint-path App Work has no prior Task (no provisioner), and nothing in APW-01, APW-03 or APW-08 creates or assigns an Agent. ACC-E2E-14 starts from 'Given a new user' (L606) and goes straight to a chat change. APW-04 creates its App Provisioner Agent only on the provisioner path (FR-7).
gaps.proposedFix: Specify in APW-08 FR-42/S25 that when no Agent resolves and the user has none, the confirmation card offers to create one from a named Agents-catalog template (with `evolve-app` bound, commit permission and an admissible runtime) and assign it to the Work. Add the matching task. Alternatively add 'user has an Agent assigned to the Work' to the ACC-E2E-07/14 preconditions.

gaps.title: Fleet-run evolve needs the GitHub App installed on the fork owner, which the create flow never sets up; the provisioner's Fleet exclusion also contradicts ACC-E2E-06
gaps.evidence: The Fleet push credential is a GitHub App installation token (EXISTING-SUBSTRATE L77; APW-08 plan L54), and APW-08 S28 fails a Fleet run with 'Install the Ever Works GitHub App on maya'. APW-01 creates forks with the member's OAuth connection (FR-15) and never prompts for or checks an installation on the target owner. The isolated sandbox is the only other admissible runtime (APW-08 FR-12). Separately, the ACC-E2E-06 and 14 preconditions accept 'an enrolled Fleet node' for the App Provisioner (ACCEPTANCE L365-366), while APW-04 plan L911 says 'Fleet nodes are excluded in P1'.
gaps.proposedFix: Add an installation check to APW-01 inspect/create for the target owner, with reason code and copy (or have APW-08 check it when the first Task starts). Correct the ACC-E2E-06/14 preconditions so the provisioner requires the restricted managed sandbox, and state separately what the evolve step accepts.

gaps.title: Drift since e5f43f44d: Fleet run-containment records and clone-URL allow-lists are not reflected in APW-08 or APW-13
gaps.evidence:
develop moved 14 non-merge commits to 873274c9f:
