gaps.title: Refusal code set and copy are incomplete: 9 codes have no copy, the ladder-off refusal and 409 have no code, and rateLimited cannot say which limit
gaps.evidence: plan.md:262-286 defines 23 UPSTREAM_REFUSAL_CODES. plan §8.1 (plan.md:483) requires one i18n key per code 'copy per spec §6.5', but spec §6.5 (spec.md:436-451) covers only 14. `notFork`, `disabled`, `sourceNotMerged`, `excludedPath`, `secretDetected`, `notSingleCommit`, `fingerprintMismatch`, `approvalExpired` and `providerUnsupported` have no copy, and ACC-E2E-04/NEG-06 expect 'the private-copy code'. `409 { code: 'activeProposal' }` (plan.md:395) is not in the list. FR-21 (spec.md:243-245) refuses when publishing is switched off, but plan.md:415 maps that to `refused / blocked`, whose copy is 'GitHub refused: your account can't open pull requests'. FR-27 requires naming which limit, but `429 { code: 'rateLimited', nextSlotAt }` has no limit discriminator. The copy 'You can open {count} pull request on {upstream} per day' fits only one of the six FR-26 limits, and 'open per upstream' has no next-slot time.
gaps.proposedFix: Add spec §6.5 rows for every code plus `activeProposal` and a new `publishingOff` code. Add `limit: keyof UPSTREAM_LIMITS` to the 429 body and one copy key per limit, with `nextSlotAt` optional for `openPerUpstream`. Update plan §3.3 and §8.1 and the T11/T22 message specs.

gaps.title: API response DTOs are named but never defined (UpstreamPullRequestView, eligibility `target`, detail view)
gaps.evidence: plan.md:375-383 returns `UpstreamPullRequestView[]`, eligibility `{ allowed, code?, nextSlotAt?, target, orgFork, maintainerCanModifyDefault }` and 'view + diff' without fields or types. T10 (tasks.md:155-156) creates `dto/upstream-pull-request.dto.ts` with no field list. Unstated: which §3.1 columns are exposed (title, body, refusalDetail, checkResults, diffStats), the `approvalProposalId` the web needs to decide, the type of `target`, the diff shape (GitDiffResult?), and where 'the member's last choice' for `maintainerCanModifyDefault` (FR-24, spec.md:256) is read from. Also missing: whether `list` returns P1 rows for other members of the Work.
gaps.proposedFix: Add `UpstreamPullRequestView`, `UpstreamEligibilityView { allowed, code?, limit?, nextSlotAt?: string, target: { owner, repo, baseBranch, forkOwner, forkRepo }, orgFork: boolean, maintainerCanModifyDefault: boolean }` and `UpstreamPullRequestDetailView` (view + `diff: GitDiffResult`, `approvalProposalId`) to plan §3.3 in contracts. Define `maintainerCanModifyDefault` as the member's most recent row's value, else true. Reference them in T10/T19.

gaps.title: Inbox notices with action buttons, and a link from the approval item to its review, are not supported by the Inbox contract; no task adds them
gaps.evidence: The spec needs notice actions: S6 **Address review** / **Open on GitHub** (spec.md:105-107), S9 **Propose** / **Dismiss** (spec.md:114-117), S17 **Open the agreement** / **I've signed it — continue** (spec.md:136-140). plan.md:457 says these use 'the existing generic notice Inbox kind', but `InboxNoticeInput` (inbox-producer.port.ts:79-101) has only title, body and ids: no actions, links or message keys. Stored title/body text cannot be translated by `dashboard.inbox.upstream.*` keys (FR-36). The approval item's Inbox mirror carries `taskId` only for merge_pull_request (agent-approvals.service.ts:219-229), so the web has no upstreamPullRequestId/workId to link to UpstreamApprovalReview (T21, tasks.md:305). Nothing names the page that hosts that component.
gaps.proposedFix: Add a task that extends the Inbox producer port additively (e.g. `InboxNoticeInput.actions?: { id, labelKey, href? | apiAction }[]` and `messageKey`/`params`), renders them in `InboxDecisionDetail`, and passes `payload.upstreamPullRequestId` plus workId for `upstream_pull_request` proposals. Name the route that mounts UpstreamApprovalReview (e.g. `/works/:id/upstream?review=<prId>`). Alternatively, scope the notices down to deep links and update the spec copy.

gaps.title: The verifier cannot compute `notSingleCommit` from getCompareDiff and may secret-scan a truncated patch
gaps.evidence: T16 (tasks.md:230-235) uses only `getCompareDiff(... { maxFiles: 300 })` for `notSingleCommit`. `GitDiffResult` (git-provider.interface.ts:453-464) has files, truncated and totals but no commit count, and github-api.service.ts:1102-1122 maps only `data.files`. Patches beyond the byte budget are dropped (`patchOmitted`, git-provider.interface.ts:445-448; default 256 KB, pr-insights.ts:22), so `assertNoSecrets` over the returned patch misses content. T16 does not refuse on `truncated`/`patchOmitted`, unlike APW-08's guard (APW-08 plan.md:246-247). `assertNoSecrets` throws a BadRequestException that embeds the matched sample (secret-scan.ts:47-55), which must not reach `refusalDetail`.
gaps.proposedFix: Add optional `GitDiffResult.totalCommits?` (mapped from compare `total_commits`) to the T1/T3 contract additions, or specify a commits read. In T16, refuse `secretDetected`/`tooLarge` when `truncated` or any `patchOmitted`, request `maxBytes: 1 MB`, use `scanForSecrets` rather than `assertNoSecrets`, and store only the pattern name.

gaps.title: The 90-minute running-time preparation deadline has no storage and no sweeper
gaps.evidence: FR-13 (spec.md:213-215) and T34 (tasks.md:427-435) count running time only, pausing on holds. plan §3.1 (plan.md:187-216) has no preparationStartedAt, pausedSince or accumulated-pause column. The status job selects only `state='open' AND nextCheckAt <= now` rows (plan.md:431), so `preparing` rows are never examined for `timedOut`. T34 modifies upstream-status.service.ts without changing that selection or naming how pause intervals are derived (run queuedReason history vs row fields).
gaps.proposedFix: Add columns `preparationStartedAt timestamptz NULL`, `preparationPausedMs bigint DEFAULT 0` and `preparationHeldSince timestamptz NULL`, with an index on `(state, preparationStartedAt)`. Extend the status job selection to `preparing` rows. Define the update points (hold start/end from `classifyAppWorkRunStop`). Update T7 and T34 accordingly.

gaps.title: The App spec schema's `upstreamPullRequests.maxOpen` (default 3) is ignored; APW-09 hard-codes 2 open per upstream
gaps.evidence: APW-03 schema.md:389-395 defines `upstreamPullRequests.maxOpen` (integer, default `3`, range 1–10) with owner APW-09. APW-09 FR-26 (spec.md:262-265) and `UPSTREAM_LIMITS.openPerUpstream: 2` (plan.md:290) never read it, and CONTRACTS §1 (CONTRACTS.md:191-193) lists only `enabled` / `requireApproval`.
gaps.proposedFix: Either have APW-09 read `maxOpen` as `min(maxOpen, UPSTREAM_LIMITS.openPerUpstream)` and document it in FR-26 and the eligibility rules, or remove or align `maxOpen` in APW-03 schema.md (default 2, max 2) and add it to CONTRACTS §1. Pin the choice in the T8 rules spec.

gaps.title: GitHub behaviours the eligibility and checks logic depend on are unverified; only the createBranchFromSha spike exists
gaps.evidence: (a) `collaboratorsOnly` detection uses `interactions.getRestrictionsForRepo` (T2/T9, tasks.md:59, 145-146). That reads temporary interaction limits, a different control from the repository-level switch restricting or disabling pull requests and the cap on outside contributors' open PRs that spec §2.3 (spec.md:59-62) cites. No refusal code exists for 'pull requests disabled', and the cap is mapped to `collaboratorsOnly` (plan.md:527). (b) FR-30 assumes `action_required` appears among check runs read by `checks.listForRef` (github-api.service.ts:986-1016). First-time-contributor approval is reported on workflow runs and check suites, so the summary may read `unknown`. (c) Interaction-limit reads with a non-admin token: 404/403 → `'none'` (tasks.md:59) would silently pass. T5 (tasks.md:84-92) spikes only createBranchFromSha.
gaps.proposedFix: Extend T5 into a P1 spike covering all three against the team-owned throwaway pair, recording results in plan §9.2. Add refusal code `pullRequestsDisabled` and an `outsideContributorCap` mapping with copy. If (b) fails, add a workflow-runs read (`getWorkflowRunForCommit` already exists) to `summarizeUpstreamChecks` inputs.

gaps.title: Provider wiring gaps: new methods not delegated in github.plugin.ts, no `head` filter for the recovery path, wrong unsupported-error type
gaps.evidence: github.plugin.ts delegates each capability explicitly to the api service (github.plugin.ts:285-353). T3 (tasks.md:64-72) adds `createBranchFromSha`/`updateBranchRef` only to github-api.service.ts, so the facade sees the methods as absent. T1 does not list github.plugin.ts either (only T2 does). plan §9.2 (plan.md:525-526) repairs a lost open via `listPullRequests(state=all, head='fork:branch')` and adopts an existing PR on 422, but `ListPullRequestsOptions` has no `head` (git-provider.interface.ts:262-266) and no task implements either failure mode. T4 (tasks.md:76) throws `GitFacadeError('providerUnsupported')`, but GitFacadeError takes (message, operation, provider) and the facade convention is `GitOperationNotSupportedError` with lazy-proxy materialisation (git.facade.ts:134-158). T3 also lacks CONTRACTS' 'whichever of APW-02/APW-09 lands first creates them' coordination (CONTRACTS.md:273).
gaps.proposedFix: Add `packages/plugins/github/src/github.plugin.ts` to T1 and T3 modify lists. Add `ListPullRequestsOptions.head?` (GitHub `head=owner:branch`) to plan §4 and T1. Add the §9.2 recovery and adopt cases to T17 tests. Change T4 to `GitOperationNotSupportedError` plus `typeof impl` materialisation, mapped to refusal `providerUnsupported`. Add an 'if APW-02 already added them, extend tests only' note to T3.

gaps.title: Label-based routing (`upstream-pr:<id>`, `upstream-candidate`) is user-writable and not bound to the row
gaps.evidence: Task `labels` are free-form and client-writable on create/update (apps/api/src/tasks/tasks.dto.ts:66-72, 228-234). plan.md:150-152 and T15 route finalize by the presence of label `upstream-pr:<id>`, without requiring `row.preparationTaskId === task.id` and `row.userId === task.userId`. So a PATCH adding that label to any App Work Task skips simulateMerge/PR and drives another row's verifier. T28 (tasks.md:376-380) treats label `upstream-candidate` as 'the Agent marked it generally useful' (FR-34), but a user can set it by hand.
gaps.proposedFix: Route finalize by row lookup (`findByPreparationTaskId` / `findByFollowUpTaskId`, same user and work) and treat the label as display only. Record the suggestion marker server-side from the tool call (e.g. Activity `app.upstream_pr.suggested` candidate or a column), not from a label. Add tests where a hand-added label changes nothing.

gaps.title: No storage for agent suggestions and dismissals (FR-34 limits, dismiss endpoint)
gaps.evidence: FR-34 (spec.md:289-291): at most 1 suggestion per Task and 3 per App Work per 7 days, and dismissed suggestions are not repeated. plan §5 adds `POST …/suggestions/:taskId/dismiss → 204` (plan.md:383) and `UPSTREAM_LIMITS.suggestionsPerWorkPer7d` (plan.md:295). plan §3.2 (plan.md:230-232) says there is no other schema change, and T28 (tasks.md:378-381) names no persistence for sent or dismissed suggestions, so the limits and the dismiss route have nothing to count or write.
gaps.proposedFix: Specify storage: a `upstream_pr_suggestions` table (workId, taskId unique, userId, sentAt, dismissedAt) with a migration in slot 01 (`1792090100000`), a R-25 backup classification and entity registration. Or explicitly count Activity `app.upstream_pr.suggested` rows and store dismissals as Activity. Update T28 and T35.

gaps.title: Approval ownership: listener 'non-author re-open' is unreachable and would collide with the unique subject key; preparation Agent choice unspecified
gaps.evidence: `createProposal` requires an Agent owned by `userId` (agent-approvals.service.ts:158-163). `decide` and `claimDecision` only accept the owning user (agent-approvals.service.ts:325, 452-460, requireOwned :499-505), so `decidedById` always equals the owner. plan.md:421-423 still says a non-author decision re-opens 'a fresh pending proposal', which would violate UNIQUE (actionType, subjectKey) (agent-action-proposal.entity.ts:128) because the fingerprint is unchanged. ACC-NEG-06 (ACCEPTANCE.md:659) expects 'approval by a non-author (stays awaiting_approval)', but the real API answers 404. T15 (tasks.md:214-220) never says which Agent runs the preparation or what happens when the member owns none; FR-35 allows any member with edit access. `expire()` (plan.md:410-411) sets status rejected; whether it emits AgentActionProposalDecidedEvent is unstated, and the listener maps rejected to withdrawn (plan.md:114).
gaps.proposedFix: State that the proposal and preparation Agent belong to the proposing member. Resolve via `APP_WORK_AGENT_RESOLVER.resolve({ userId: member, workId })` and return `409 agentRequired` when null. Remove the re-open logic. Change ACC-NEG-06's non-author case to 'another user's approval id → 404, no create call'. Specify that `expire` emits no decided event (or the listener branches on `decidedVia === 'expired'` → state `expired`).

gaps.title: Preparation dispatch: no mechanism for 'Fleet refused', no named brief vehicle, and no ordering against APW-08's AppChangeGuard
gaps.evidence: T15 (tasks.md:219-220) says 'dispatchAgentRun (APW-08 isolated admission; Fleet refused)'. APW-08 T12 admits Fleet runs as isolated (APW-08 tasks.md:212-214), and routing to a Fleet happens inside the job runtime adapter from tenant config (task-transition.service.ts:1063-1075), so no hook for refusing Fleet is named. The 'source PR diff (≤ 256 KB) and guide files (≤ 64 KB each) attached to the brief' has no vehicle: Task description, `pendingInput` (task-transition.service.ts:871-893), or a file. APW-08 T17 calls AppChangeGuard in `finalizeRun` before openPullRequestForBranch (APW-08 tasks.md:295-296), comparing against the fork base. T15 does not say its early branch must precede the guard, whose compare of an upstream-based branch would refuse.
gaps.proposedFix: Name the Fleet refusal (e.g. dispatch with a `delegationScope`/execution preference that the Fleet dispatcher refuses, as review runs are). Name the brief vehicle, `pendingInput` fenced entries with byte caps, since untrusted content is never put in the system prompt. State that the upstream-pr finalize branch runs before AppChangeGuard and simulateMerge. Add T15 test cases for all three.

gaps.title: Upstream PR limits are per member only; no per-upstream cap, maintainer opt-out or platform deny list
gaps.evidence: APW-09 FR-26 (spec lines 262-265) limits each member to 1 PR per upstream per day and 3 overall. With many members or organizations the same popular upstream can receive unbounded PRs from the platform. Detecting 'no AI contributions' is an open question (line 510). There is no platform-wide cap per upstream repository, no way for a maintainer to opt out (for example a repository topic or file), and no operator deny list or kill switch.
gaps.proposedFix: Add FRs for a platform-wide cap per upstream per day, honouring a maintainer opt-out marker, an operator deny list (admin route) and the XC-10 switch; add refusal codes, copy and ACCs.

gaps.title: The quarantine and release handshake between Work.spec and Work.status is undefined
gaps.evidence: `setDesiredState(workId, 'running'|'quarantined', q?)` (plan.md:474) carries a request id only for quarantine (spec.quarantine, plan.md:235); release has none. A detector quarantine is written only to `status.quarantine.source=detector`, and 'the platform mirrors it' (plan.md:188-190), but the platform credential can only read status (plan.md:296-297) and nothing says whether the mirror writes `spec.desiredState`. So an operator release of a detector quarantine (setting `running`, which spec already says) gives the controller nothing to act on. `deployApp → applyWork` (plan.md:506) could write `desiredState: running` over an active quarantine. T26 (tasks.md:431-433) keys cancellation on `observedGeneration < generation` without saying whether that means `spec.generation` or `metadata.generation`; a quarantine patch bumps metadata.generation. S19's 'release waits for an applying quarantine' (spec.md:158-160) has no mechanism.
gaps.proposedFix: Add `spec.release: { requestId, requestedAt }`. The platform mirror sets `spec.desiredState: quarantined` with `quarantine.requestId` equal to the detector's status requestId. The mapper never touches desiredState or quarantine (add a test). `observedGeneration` refers to `spec.generation`. Define S19: release returns 409 `APPS_TIER_QUARANTINE_APPLYING` until `ingressDisabledAt` is set, or the service queues it. Update T7, T17 and T26 tests accordingly.

gaps.title: FR-32's single-use 15-minute pull credential contradicts the credential APW-05 actually provides
gaps.evidence: spec.md:316-317 (FR-32) requires private images to be pulled 'with a single-use credential … valid for at most 15 minutes', and plan.md:240 carries `pullCredential.expiresAt ≤ 15 min`. APW-05 plan.md:807-819 implements `AppImagePullCredentialSource` as the user's classic token with exactly `read:packages` scope, whose expiry comes from GitHub; APW-06's port returns `{server, username, password}` with no TTL. Nothing mints a short-lived token, so `expiresAt` is only a label on a long-lived credential that can read every package the user can.
gaps.proposedFix: Either change FR-32 and plan §3.1 to 'a read-only registry credential sealed to the controller, used only by the promotion Job, never written into a tenant namespace and discarded after the copy' (and test that the discard happens), or add a CONTRACTS row asking APW-05 for a short-lived pull token and name its task.

gaps.title: FR-23's check for organization credentials cannot be implemented: nothing produces their fingerprints
gaps.evidence: FR-23 (spec.md:276-278) says no credential issued to an organization ever reaches a tenant, enforced by matching env values against 'configured platform credential fingerprints'. plan.md:369 keeps the HMAC key and fingerprint list in a zone Secret that the platform can neither read nor write (Role, plan.md:292-311). Organization credentials (Git connections, org tokens, plugin settings) are created and rotated at runtime in the platform database. No task or hook computes, pushes or refreshes their fingerprints; T5 (tasks.md:119-121) tests only against 'a configured fingerprint'.
gaps.proposedFix: Choose and document a population path. Option A: a platform-held fingerprint key (new env var in CONTRACTS §7), fingerprints computed on credential create or rotate and written as a namespaced `CredentialFingerprintSet` custom resource (added to the platform Role), with the controller reading that list. Option B: narrow FR-23's matching to operator-configured platform credentials and state that organization credentials are excluded by construction (tenant env comes only from APW-07's per-App-Work store). Add a task and a test either way.

gaps.title: The sealed payload has no defined byte format and is not tied to one Work
gaps.evidence: plan.md:101 (D-D) names only the algorithms (RSA-OAEP-256 4096-bit + AES-256-GCM). plan.md:247 (`env.sealed`) and plan.md:240 (`pullCredential.sealed`) are opaque base64. T12 (tasks.md:204-216) seals in the plugin and T5 (tasks.md:113-121) unseals in the controller — two packages — and requires a round trip, but no envelope layout (key id, wrapped key, IV and tag lengths, encoding) or additional authenticated data is defined. Because the ciphertext is not bound to a workId, field and generation, anyone who can write Work objects could copy one Work's sealed env or pull credential into another Work and the zone would unseal it.
gaps.proposedFix: Define the envelope in `packages/contracts/src/apps/apps-tier-seal.ts`: `{ v: 1, kid, alg: 'RSA-OAEP-256+A256GCM', ek, iv (12 bytes), tag (16 bytes), ct }` as base64url JSON, with AAD = `hosting.ever.works/v1alpha1|<workId>|<field>`. The controller refuses a mismatch with SEALED_PAYLOAD_INVALID. Add a committed golden test vector fixture used by both T5 and T12.

gaps.title: The apps-tier capability's types are unnamed, and the interface lacks methods the tasks need
gaps.evidence: T2 (tasks.md:74-75) says 'exactly as plan §5.1', but plan.md:469-488 only names AppsTierZoneInfo, AppsTierWorkDesiredState, AppsTierWorkStatus, AppsTierQuarantineRequest, AppsTierSelfCheckStatus, AppsTierAccessReview, AppsTierUsageReport, AppsTierAbuseSignalReport, AppsTierBuildRequest and AppsTierBuildStatus, without fields. Admin `GET works` (plan.md:638) and Pause all (FR-44) need a list of tier Works, but the interface has only `getWork(workId)`. T23 (tasks.md:378) projects image allowances with no interface method. `getHeartbeat()` returns `controllerVersion` (plan.md:480), but the platform can read only the Lease (plan.md:308-311), which has no version field. `AppsTierFacadeService` (plan.md:530) must work in system jobs with no user, but BaseFacadeService methods require FacadeOptions with a userId (`packages/agent/src/facades/base.facade.ts:57-71`).
gaps.proposedFix: Write out each type in plan §5.1, derived field by field from the §3.1-3.2 CRD shapes. Add `listWorks({ phase?, limit, continueToken })` and `setImageAllowances(workId, allowances)`. Say where controllerVersion comes from (e.g. Lease annotation `hosting.ever.works/controller-version` or zone-info). Specify how the facade resolves the plugin outside a user context (installation-level enablement by operator env or admin settings, no userId).

gaps.title: Removal completion with APW-06 and cleanup of retained Work objects are unowned
gaps.evidence: APW-06 plan.md:969-980 (§9.7) deprovisions dependencies first, then calls `destroyApp` → `removeWork` (which returns void, plan.md:476), then immediately calls `completeAppWorkDeletion`, which deletes the Work row. APW-10 plan.md:205-209 deletes stored data only after `status.dependencies[]` reports `released`, and says 'the platform deletes the Work object only after dataDeletedAt is set or the 30-day retention was cleared'. No job or task performs that deletion, and once the Work row is gone nothing on the platform tracks the retained object. The `AppDestroyResult.kept[]` that APW-06 records for ever-works-apps is never mapped in T26 or T39.
gaps.proposedFix: In T39, define `destroyApp` → `{ kept: [{ kind: 'PersistentVolumeClaim'|'Dependency', name }] }` from `getWork` status. Add a gate-watch step or a new `apps-tier-removal-gc` task that lists Removed Work objects with `dataDeletedAt` set, or past `retainedUntil` once the operator has cleared them, and deletes them, with a test. State the ordering against APW-06 step 1 in CONTRACTS row 276.

gaps.title: Task file lists miss required registry and config edits, and duplicate edits owned by APW-03 and APW-05
gaps.evidence: T16 (tasks.md:267-272) binds the dispatcher 'like every other *_DISPATCHER' but modifies only `_tasks-symbols.ts` and `index.ts`. Binding also needs `packages/agent/src/tasks/job-runtime.providers.ts` DISPATCHER_SYMBOLS (arity pinned at 14 in `__tests__/job-runtime.providers.spec.ts:134-143`), `packages/tasks/src/trigger/trigger.service.ts` and `trigger.module.ts`. T1 (tasks.md:64-66) may create the `apps` area without listing `packages/contracts/src/__tests__/index.barrel.spec.ts` (AREAS and count, :106). `git grep EVER_WORKS_APPS_` outside docs/specs finds nothing, and no task adds the six APW-10 env vars (CONTRACTS.md:395, 409-413) to `packages/agent/src/config/index.ts` or env examples, although T27's Done-when (tasks.md:455-456) allows reads only there. T25 adds `works.appsTierQuotaProfile` without `packages/agent/src/entities/work.entity.ts`. Meanwhile T31 (tasks.md:506-513) repeats APW-03 T23/T24, whose mapper is already pure and reads APPS_TIER_POLICY (APW-03 tasks.md:325-351), so T31's Done-when is always true; T35 (tasks.md:555-557) repeats APW-05 T35's `build.facade.ts` edit (APW-05 tasks.md:488-490).
gaps.proposedFix: Add the missing Modify entries, including the arity edit from 14 to 15 and the barrel AREAS update. Add a config task creating an `everWorks.appsTier` config section with the CONTRACTS defaults and the env examples. Add `work.entity.ts` to T25. Turn T31 and T35 into verification-only steps that cite APW-03 T24 and APW-05 T35.

gaps.title: Quota profiles cannot reach the zone within FR-48's 5 minutes, and the profile fields are undefined
gaps.evidence: plan.md:370: the ConfigMap `ever-works-apps-quota-profiles` is 'pushed from the platform's profile table by the operator runbook'. The platform Role can only `get` two other named ConfigMaps (plan.md:304-307). FR-48 (spec.md:376-378) promises edits apply within 5 minutes. plan.md:446 gives `limits simple-json (FR-47 fields)` without field names or units, and a `buildMinutesMonthly` column that FR-47 gives no seed value for. The ceilings (16 CPU, 32 GiB, 100 pods, 500 GiB; T25 tasks.md:410-411) don't say whether CPU and memory mean requests or limits, and set no bandwidth or egress ceiling. The body of `PUT quota-profiles/:name` (plan.md:646) is just 'limits'.
gaps.proposedFix: Define `AppsTierQuotaLimits` in contracts (cpuRequest, cpuLimit, memoryRequestMiB, memoryLimitMiB, pods, volumes, storageGiB, bandwidthOutMbit, bandwidthInMbit, monthlyEgressGiB, buildMinutesMonthly) with seed values, 0 for build minutes until P3. Have the plugin carry the resolved limits inside `Work.spec.quotaProfile` on every applyWork and re-apply assigned Works after an edit, or grant the Role `update` on that ConfigMap and add a sync step with a test. State that the ceilings bound limits.

gaps.title: Operator and owner API responses are unnamed, and the refusal reason can't list the failing items
gaps.evidence: plan.md:628-655 describes returns only as 'runs', 'events', 'signals', 'attestation', `{ state, scope, reasons, lastRun, heartbeat, items[] }`, 'tier App Works with profile, phase, 24 h CPU, 30 d egress, open signals', and `usage30d`: no field names or types, no cursor format, no owner email masking rule. evaluate() pushes `RUN_NOT_GREEN` with no item ids (plan.md:553), while the 409 body is `[{ code, items? }]` and S9 and §6.1 copy need 'Self-check failed (LG-07, LG-13)' (spec.md:130-131, 463). No DTO file is named for the owner controller (T30). T19's controller spec and T20's pages cannot be written against a fixed shape.
gaps.proposedFix: Add a response table to plan §6 with types in `packages/contracts/src/apps/apps-tier.ts`: AppsTierStatusResponse, AppsTierGateItemView {id, titleKey, kind, phase, outcome, reasonCode, durationMs, attestation?}, AppsTierRunSummary, AppsTierWorkRow {workId, workName, ownerMasked, profile, phase, cpuHours24h, egressGiB30d, openSignals}, AppsTierSignalView, WorkAppsTierView. Use an opaque base64 `(finishedAt, id)` cursor. Make `RUN_NOT_GREEN` carry `items: string[]`. Add `apps/api/src/apps-tier/dto/apps-tier-user.dto.ts` to T30.

gaps.title: Eligibility rules are underspecified: 'paid subscription' has no definition and the per-person cap overlaps APW-06's quota
gaps.evidence: FR-35 (spec.md:329-331) requires 'an active paid subscription'. `SubscriptionService.getActiveSubscription` (subscription.service.ts:384) returns any active subscription, and plans carry `monthlyPrice`, `annualPrice` and `hosting` (subscription-plan.entity.ts:38, 73) with no 'paid' rule; behaviour when subscriptions are disabled is unstated. plan.md:523 (eligibility service) leaves out the cap, while T27 (tasks.md:440-442) includes 'per-person cap' and plan.md:580 has the reason code `capReached`, but no cap source is named. CONTRACTS.md:397 gives `EVER_WORKS_APPS_MAX_PER_USER` to APW-06, whose `EverWorksAppsQuotaService` refuses with `quota_exceeded` (APW-06 tasks.md:621-627). The same condition would get two codes.
gaps.proposedFix: Define `isPaidSubscription`: active, plan.hosting === 'cloud', and monthlyPrice > 0 or annualPrice > 0. State behaviour when subscriptions are disabled. Remove `capReached` from APW-10 eligibility and defer to APW-06's `quota_exceeded`, or name `EVER_WORKS_APPS_MAX_PER_USER` as the single source with a mapping between the codes. Update T27's test cases.

gaps.title: The zone controller's inputs for usage, abuse signals and the sandbox check have no defined shape
gaps.evidence: `usage-reporter.ts` does 'hourly aggregation' and `signal-rules.ts` implements 'FR-38 heuristics' (plan.md:420-421), with a 'runtime sensor intake adapter (sensor named in zone config)' (T28, T29 at tasks.md:459, 476-477). Nothing defines where per-pod CPU core-seconds, memory, egress bytes, PVC GiB-hours, per-port refused-connection counts or sensor events come from, or their shape, so T28/T29 unit fixtures can't be written against a contract. The LG-04 probe (plan.md:379) matches 'the kernel signature of the sandbox', but zone-info (plan.md:366) carries only `sandboxRuntimeClass`, so the probe has no signature to match. FR-36 throttles 'until the next month', but no task clears `egressThrottle` when the month starts.
gaps.proposedFix: Define controller ports: `UsageMetricsSource.window(workId, start, end) → { cpuCoreSeconds, memoryMiBHours, egressMiB, storageGiBHours }`, `FlowEventSource.refusedConnections(namespace, window) → Array<{ port, count }>`, and `RuntimeSensorEvent { namespace, ruleId, severity, observedAt, summary }`, each selected by zone config and each with a fake. Add `sandboxKernelSignature` (a regex) to zone-info. Add a monthly unthrottle step with a test to T28.

gaps.title: T3's CRD test asserts rejections a CRD cannot perform
gaps.evidence: T3 (tasks.md:92-94) says the `Work` CRD 'rejects a `namespace` field … and an object over 512 KiB'. plan.md:264 claims 'a CRD `x-kubernetes-validations` size rule'. CEL validation rules cannot measure an object's serialized size, and a structural schema silently drops unknown fields instead of rejecting them unless the client asks for strict field validation. `crds.spec.ts` is a Vitest unit spec with no API server, and no validator is named to evaluate the generated schema.
gaps.proposedFix: Have T3's test check sample objects against the generated openAPIV3Schema with ajv (`ajv@8.18.0` is in node_modules): `additionalProperties: false` on spec and the `@sha256:` pattern. Move the 512 KiB and namespace-field refusals to T5's `work-spec.validator.spec.ts` and the zone admission policy. In plan §3.1, replace the 'CRD size rule' claim with per-field maxLength/maxItems bounds.

gaps.title: T20's 'mocked API' Playwright specs cannot mock these server-rendered admin pages
gaps.evidence: T20 (tasks.md:326-340) requires `apps/web/e2e/admin-apps-tier-gate.spec.ts` and `admin-apps-tier-quarantine.spec.ts` 'with a mocked API', with pages that follow `admin/usage/page.tsx`. That page fetches on the server (`adminUsageAPI.list()` at page.tsx:53, then `notFound()`), which Playwright's page.route cannot intercept. flow-subscription-admin-usage.spec.ts:24-29 notes that no default e2e user is a platform admin; admin-tenant-runtime-allowlist.spec.ts:105-121 registers an `e2e-admin-*` user instead. The e2e API has no apps-tier plugin or zone, and plan.md:530 throws AppsTierUnavailableError without saying what `GET status` returns then.
gaps.proposedFix: Specify the e2e setup: register an `e2e-admin-*` platform admin; bind a fake apps-tier provider in the e2e API behind a non-production env flag (added to CONTRACTS §7), or have the board fetch on the client through `apps/web/src/lib/api/admin-apps-tier.ts` so page.route works. Define `GET status` with no enabled plugin as state closed, reason `ZONE_NOT_CONFIGURED`.

gaps.title: Tier data model gaps: the self-check single-run guard has no index, retention has no task, and columns lack types
gaps.evidence: Only one self-check may run at a time, enforced 'via the running row' (plan.md:520, T16), but `apps_tier_gate_runs` has only the index `(status, finishedAt)` (plan.md:441). Two simultaneous POSTs can both insert, and T16's test is sequential. FR-9's retention (180 days or the latest 500 runs, spec.md:232-234) has no task. Many columns lack type, length or nullability: `trigger`, `status`, `scope`, `category`, `source`, `kind`, `severity`, `zoneName`, `ruleId`, allowance `reason`, and `pluginUsageEventId` (plan.md:441-449). The partial unique indexes have no MySQL/MariaDB fallback; the precedent `1791240000000-AddSafetyRailsCore.ts:289-307` falls back to a service-level check. Program rule 2: the new tables AppsTierImageAllowance and AppsTierUsageWindow are not justified in spec §5.2, and T37 (tasks.md:575-578) leaves 'Tier state change' out of README §1.
gaps.proposedFix: Add a partial unique index on `apps_tier_gate_runs(status) WHERE status = 'running'`, with a concurrency test. Add a retention step with a test to gate-watch. Give every column a type, length and nullability (e.g. varchar(16) enums, `zoneName` varchar(253) unique, uuid ids). Define the fallback on engines without partial indexes. Justify the two tables in spec §5.2 and add all spec §5.2 nouns to README §1 in the same PRs as T13/T25.

gaps.title: Managed quota numbers disagree between APW-06 and APW-10, and Cal.diy's shape exceeds the default Starter profile
gaps.evidence: APW-06 FR-22 (spec L313-317) and plan §4.2 (L322-324) give managed quota as requests 2 CPU / 4 GiB, limits 4 CPU / 6 GiB, 20 pods, 5 PVCs, 20 GiB. APW-10 FR-47 (spec L372-375) gives Starter as 1/2 CPU, 2/4 GiB, 10 pods, 4 volumes, 10 GiB and Standard as 2/4 CPU, 4/8 GiB, 20 pods, 8 volumes, 50 GiB; `appsTierQuotaProfile` NULL means Starter (plan L449). Cal.diy's web container has a 3Gi memory limit (works.yml L89), and its pre-deploy `migrate` job reuses the web component's resources (L161-165). Under Starter's 4 GiB limit, a running web pod plus the migrate Job (6 GiB), or a rolling surge (6 GiB), is refused by the quota, so every Deployment after the first fails.
gaps.proposedFix: Make APW-10 FR-47 the single source and have APW-06 FR-22 reference the assigned profile (via `AppsTierPolicy.podPolicy()`). Add a render-time precondition `quota_insufficient` that sums peak usage (components + surge + pre-deploy jobs) against the profile. Give Blueprints an optional job `resources` override so migrate jobs need less memory.

gaps.title: Pricing and credits for hosting, builds and provisioning are undecided, and the pricebook citation is wrong
gaps.evidence: APW-10 spec leaves credit prices per hosting unit and the Starter/Standard cost open; README question 3 defaults Wave 2 to verified, paying accounts, but no plan or entitlement change is specified. APW-10 plan 5.3 and its metering task add five hosting.* keys at 0 to packages/agent/src/usage/credit-price-list.ts, which is only the port; the table is the frozen, versioned packages/agent/src/subscriptions/billing/credit-pricebook.ts (a new key needs a new version), and existing keys use camelCase operations (mcp.toolCall) while APW-10 uses hosting.cpu_core_hour. README rule 12 receipts for Builds and Provisioner runs have no recorded pricing decision.
gaps.proposedFix: Owner sets hosting prices, quota profile costs and eligibility (plan or entitlement); fix the APW-10 plan and task citation to a pricebook version 2 in credit-pricebook.ts with camelCase operation keys; add a billing task if paying accounts are required.

gaps.title: Tile name never reads APW-03's displayName, but acceptance expects '(community build)' names
gaps.evidence: ACCEPTANCE.md:640 (E2E-14) expects 'App Launcher lists **Cal.diy (community build)** with the live URL', and :549 (E2E-12) lists 'the App Work by its display name'. APW-03 plan.md:360 lists APW-11 consuming `WorkAppSpecState.displayName` as the 'launcher label', and CONTRACTS.md:230 names APW-11 as a consumer of WorkAppSpecState. APW-11 plan §3.3 has `name: string // ≤ 100` with no source, and no APW-11 file mentions displayName (grep). An implementer would use Work.name and E2E-14 would fail.
gaps.proposedFix: State in plan §4.1 step 4/5 and T6 that item.name = WorkAppSpecState.displayName when set (kind app), else Work.name, capped at 100. Add a T6 test row, and list WorkAppSpecState in the plan header's consumed contracts.

gaps.title: Deployment state to chip mapping (Deploying / Last deploy failed) is undefined
gaps.evidence: spec FR-18 requires the chips. plan.md:333-336 says only that findLatestForWorks is used 'for chips'. States at HEAD: INITIALIZING default (work-deployment.entity.ts:65), BUILDING/QUEUED (apps/api/src/plugins-capabilities/deploy/tasks/deployment-verifier.service.ts:13-16), terminal READY/ERROR/CANCELED/TIMEOUT. APW-06 plan.md:622-624 and :702 add DEPLOYING, VERIFYING, ROLLED_BACK and SUPERSEDED. ACCEPTANCE.md:664 (NEG-11) requires a rolled-back App Work to show 'Last deploy failed'. No document says which states mean `deploying`, which mean `lastDeployFailed` (is CANCELED a failure? is a SUPERSEDED latest row?), or whether the chip uses the latest row or the latest non-superseded one.
gaps.proposedFix: Add a table to plan §4.1 and to T4/T6: deploying = {INITIALIZING, QUEUED, BUILDING, DEPLOYING, VERIFYING}; lastDeployFailed = {ERROR, TIMEOUT, ROLLED_BACK} (decide CANCELED); ignore SUPERSEDED when choosing 'latest'. Pin it in app-launcher.service.spec.ts.

gaps.title: features.appLauncherEnabled breaks the pinned /api/config contract, has no web reader, and parses booleans differently from the guard
gaps.evidence: T9 (tasks.md:204-205) adds features.appLauncherEnabled. apps/web/e2e/flow-config-public-contract.spec.ts:120-125 asserts the exact sorted feature keys [anonymousAuthEnabled, emailVerificationRequired, magicLinkEnabled, subscriptionsEnabled], and T9 does not update it. T13 reads the flag 'from the public API config', but no web code reads /api/config at HEAD (git grep in apps/web/src), and T13 gives no fetch helper, timeout or cache. `truthy()` in apps/api/src/api.controller.ts:93 accepts 'true'/'1'/'yes', while the guard in tasks.md:188-189 requires === 'true'. With the env set to '1' the web shows the control and every API call answers 404.
gaps.proposedFix: In T9, update flow-config-public-contract.spec.ts and api.controller.spec.ts (the it.each rows), and make the guard and config use one parser (a `config.appLauncher.isEnabled()` accessor). In T13, name the reader: a server-only fetch of `${API_URL}/api/config` with a timeout and fail-closed default, or read the same env server-side as apps/web/src/lib/fleet-flags.ts does.

gaps.title: Flag plumbing misses the nested settings layout and the Work settings page
gaps.evidence: T13 (tasks.md:258-259) computes the flag in (dashboard)/layout.tsx and passes it 'to DashboardHeader, the palette context and the settings layout'. The settings nav is rendered by the nested server layout apps/web/src/app/[locale]/(dashboard)/settings/layout.tsx (:1-25, which already computes fleetEnabled itself). A parent App Router layout cannot pass props into it. T16 modifies only settings-layout-client.tsx. T17 needs the flag in GeneralSettings, but the chain works/[id]/settings/page.tsx → SettingsForm.tsx → GeneralSettings is not listed for modification.
gaps.proposedFix: Add settings/layout.tsx (call isAppLauncherEnabled and pass `appLauncherEnabled` to SettingsLayoutClient) to T16. Add works/[id]/settings/page.tsx and SettingsForm.tsx (or SettingsProvider context) to T17, with the prop name and its default of false.

gaps.title: apps/web never declares @ever-works/app-launcher in P1, so the Docker web build prunes it
gaps.evidence: T10 creates packages/app-launcher, and T14 does `import('@ever-works/app-launcher')`. Only T28 (P2, tasks.md:455) modifies apps/web/package.json. apps/web/package.json:37-38 declares workspace packages explicitly. .deploy/docker/web/Dockerfile:61/95/102 builds from a turbo-pruned tree (`out/json`, `out/full`, `turbo build --filter=ever-works-web...`), so an undeclared workspace package is neither linked nor built, and the web build fails to resolve the import.
gaps.proposedFix: Add to T10 or T14: modify apps/web/package.json with `"@ever-works/app-launcher": "workspace:*"`. Add a Done-when: `turbo build --filter=ever-works-web...` builds the package first.

gaps.title: Lit bundling is undecided, so the 30 KB size check is vacuous and P2 static fixtures cannot load dist/index.js
gaps.evidence: T10 (tasks.md:218-221) builds with tsup, lists `lit` as a dependency, and checks gzip of dist/index.js ≤ 30,720 bytes for ACC-11-35 / FR-46 ('the component, including its styles'). tsup leaves package.json dependencies out of the bundle by default, and packages/*/tsup.config.ts has no noExternal precedent, so dist/index.js would omit Lit and the check measures the wrong artifact. T27 (tasks.md:440-442) loads dist/index.js from static HTML fixture pages, where the bare `lit` import cannot resolve. `lit` and `happy-dom` are absent from pnpm-lock.yaml, and no licence note covers the new dependencies.
gaps.proposedFix: State in plan §6.1 and T10: `noExternal: ['lit']` (single self-contained ESM file), or lit as a peer plus a documented import map. Make check-size measure the file consumers load. Add lit and happy-dom as devDependency/dependency lines with a licence note, and give T27 fixture pages a concrete loading method.

gaps.title: Pin order, pin limit across global and per-Organization rows, and reorder writes are underspecified
gaps.evidence: FR-25 caps pins at 6 per person per Organization, counting Ever apps (scopeKey 'global', shared by all Organizations) plus Works. Pinning a global item while in Org B can leave Org A with 7 pins, and no document says how the panel or Manage apps handles that. plan.md:357-361 says 'recompute pin orders', but pinOrder 0..5 lives on both the shared global rows and the per-scope rows (plan.md:205) with no merge or collision rule. AppLauncherPreferenceChange (plan.md:276-281) has no pinOrder, so pins cannot be reordered. Move up/down from default ordering (sortOrder NULL: newest READY deployment first) must write explicit orders for a whole section, but no algorithm is given. Manage apps must list 'every eligible item' (FR-27) while candidates reach 500 and responses and saves cap at 200 (plan.md:319-320, 349), with no pagination.
gaps.proposedFix: In plan §4.2, specify: pinOrder is computed per (global ∪ scopeKey) view at read time, and stored pinOrder is ignored or recomputed; what happens when another Organization exceeds 6 (show the first 6 by pin time); whether a pinOrder change field exists; that a move writes sortOrder for every item in the section; and pagination or an explicit cap message for Manage apps beyond 200. Add matching T4/T6 test rows.

gaps.title: Reset-to-default (null) exposure and the Activity row fields are undefined
gaps.evidence: plan.md:379-387 accepts `appLauncherExposed: null` (reset to kind default) but defines only `app.launcher.exposed`/`hidden` and `metadata: { explicit }`. It does not say which action a null write logs, or whether 'changed' compares the stored value or the effective one (for example null→true on an `app` Work). Web telemetry has `direction: 'on'|'off'|'default'` (plan.md:669). CreateActivityLogDto requires `status` and `summary` (packages/agent/src/entities/activity-log.types.ts:427-433), and T7 specifies neither (the summary text, and whether it is localized). FR-21 requires the 'direction' in the record.
gaps.proposedFix: In plan §4.4 and T7: the action follows the effective value after the write; the no-op rule compares effective exposure plus the explicit flag; status = ActivityStatus.COMPLETED; give an exact English summary template (no name, no address); metadata `{ explicit: boolean, previousEffective: boolean }`. Add test rows for null.

gaps.title: Empty-state actions (Create an App Work / Go to Works) have no data signal, element event or route
gaps.evidence: spec S8 (spec.md:121-123) shows 'Create an App Work' when App Works are available to the person, otherwise 'Go to Works'. AppLauncherListResponse.meta (plan.md:263-274) carries no App Works availability (APW-01's fail-closed `works-app` flag / EVER_WORKS_APP_WORKS_ENABLED, R-6), and the element properties carry none. The element API (plan.md:522-539) has events open/close/item-activate/manage/sign-in/retry only, so a host cannot react to either button, and no document names the target routes.
gaps.proposedFix: Add `meta.appWorksAvailable: boolean` (or a host-fed element property) and an event such as `ever-app-launcher:empty-action` with detail `{ action: 'createAppWork' | 'goToWorks' }`. Name the routes in plan §6.4 (the APW-01 create route with kind app, and ROUTES for Works), and add T12/T14 tests.

gaps.title: No task adds launcher env vars to the deploy manifests, and the catalog ENV default would show production addresses on stage and dev
gaps.evidence: API env is enumerated per variable with `$VAR` substitution in .deploy/k8s/k8s-manifest.{dev,stage,prod}.yaml (for example stage :291-294 EVER_WORKS_DOMAIN). CONTRACTS.md:407 defaults EVER_WORKS_PLATFORM_CATALOG_ENV to `production`. T23 (tasks.md:388-389) only says 'enable EVER_WORKS_APP_LAUNCHER_ENABLED=true on stage', and T18's Done-when needs `EVER_WORKS_PLATFORM_CATALOG_REF=v1.0.0 on stage`. No task names the manifest files. Deployed unchanged, stage and dev would read `production` URLs, which contradicts FR-10 ('never sends a person from one environment to another').
gaps.proposedFix: Add a T23 pre-step (or a T9 sub-step) that modifies the three k8s manifests with EVER_WORKS_APP_LAUNCHER_ENABLED and EVER_WORKS_PLATFORM_CATALOG_{REPO,REF,ENV,SELF_ID} (ENV = develop/stage/production per file), plus apps/api/.env.example. Consider failing boot or logging an error when ENV is unset outside production.

gaps.title: The platform catalog location and first entries need the owner, and T18/T23 cannot finish without them
gaps.evidence: spec.md:583-591 keeps [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] on where the catalog repository lives (ever-works vs ever-co) and which platforms are in the first catalog ('Ever Rec and others need a named owner per entry'). T18 (tasks.md:327-337) is 'owner action … requires the owner's go-ahead on spec §9 question 1' with 'owner-supplied addresses per environment'. T23's Done-when ('EVER_WORKS_PLATFORM_CATALOG_REF=v1.0.0 on stage renders three tiles', 'all 33 ticked on stage') depends on it. P1 code tasks can proceed on the default.
gaps.proposedFix: Owner confirms the ever-works/platforms location (or the alternative), the first entries with a named owner each, and the per-environment addresses, which live only in that repository and never in this public spec.

gaps.title: App Work address and liveness ignore APW-06's primary domain and paused/removed/quarantined state
gaps.evidence: spec FR-16 (spec.md:211-214) and plan §4.6 pick the earliest-added verified production custom domain. APW-06 spec.md:386 FR-38 and plan.md:755-757 define an App Work's primary address as 'the verified custom domain the owner marked primary (targetSettings.primaryDomain)'. For App Works the launcher would open a different domain from the one the app publishes as primary. CONTRACTS.md:233-234 list APW-11 as a consumer of the WorkDeployment extensions and WorkAppRuntimeState ('paused/removed', 'current Deployment'), but APW-11 reads neither. A paused or removed App Work (APW-06 app-lifecycle) or a quarantined one (APW-10) keeps an old READY row and would still be listed as live.
gaps.proposedFix: For kind `app`, have T6 resolve the address from APW-06's published primary host and treat WorkAppRuntimeState paused/removed (and APW-10 quarantine) as not live. Keep FR-16's earliest-domain rule for other kinds, and state both rules in spec FR-15 and FR-16. Add rows to T6's service spec.

gaps.title: Platform catalog ever-works/platforms is not drafted beyond an inline example
gaps.evidence: gh api GET repos/ever-works/platforms returns 404. APW-11 plan 5.1 gives the layout, one JSON example and the zod rules; T18 is an owner action. No platforms.schema.json, validation workflow, README, CONTRIBUTING or icons are drafted; per-environment URLs are owner-supplied. README section 1 names Rec as a launcher destination, but T18 seeds only Ever Works, Gauzy and Teams.
gaps.proposedFix: Draft docs/specs/features/app-works/APW-11-app-launcher/platforms-catalog-draft/ with platforms.json (URL placeholders), schema/platforms.schema.json mirroring the zod rules, a validate script and workflow (24 entries, 16 KB icons, https only, unique ids), README, CONTRIBUTING and LICENSE; owner supplies URLs and icons, decides Rec, and creates the repository.

gaps.title: Replay-store cleanup SQL fails on MySQL/MariaDB, which the platform supports
gaps.evidence: plan.md:221-225 deletes expired rows with `DELETE … WHERE id IN (SELECT id … LIMIT 100)` and calls it 'portable to Postgres and SQLite'. The platform also wires mysql and mariadb (packages/agent/src/database/database.config.ts:33-34, 208-211). Commit b5a7d6857, one of the 14 that landed after the program was verified, fixed exactly this class of portability bug for those engines. MySQL and MariaDB reject LIMIT inside an IN subquery and a subquery on the table being deleted from.
gaps.proposedFix: Specify a query that works on all four engines. For example, select up to 100 expired ids in one query, then run DELETE … WHERE id IN (:ids). Add a repository or service spec note covering mysql.

gaps.title: Adding the 'identity' plugin category breaks the web type-check; T4 omits that file
gaps.evidence: T4 (tasks.md:82-90) appends 'identity' to PLUGIN_CATEGORIES, and its Done-when checks only that the plugin package builds. apps/web/src/lib/utils/plugin-category-icons.ts:33 and 79 declare exhaustive Record<PluginCategory, …> maps, and lines 108-109 assert every category has an icon and a label. The root type-check in T34 would fail.
gaps.proposedFix: Add apps/web/src/lib/utils/plugin-category-icons.ts (icon and label for 'identity', plus any label i18n) to T4's Modify list, and make root type-check part of T4's Done-when.

gaps.title: Node sign-in with Ever ID has no user-facing caller
gaps.evidence: FR-39 (spec.md:281-284) says nodes can sign in with device authorization. T29 (tasks.md:338-342) and plan.md:633-635 change only apps/node/src/core/auth-client.ts and runtime.ts. The only caller of node credential sign-in is the desktop app (apps/desktop-node/src/main/main.ts:261-268, enrollNodeWithCredentials with email and password), and no task adds a device-code path or a prompt that shows the code there. The node half of ACC-12-28 cannot be observed by a person.
gaps.proposedFix: Add a task for apps/desktop-node: a new enroll mode, IPC, and a renderer prompt showing the verification address and code. If the Ever ID path is CLI-only for nodes, say so and name the node CLI entry point and its test.

gaps.title: The delegated-apps list on the card has no source for app names, the 'Manage in Ever ID' link or the 30-day window
gaps.evidence: FR-48 (spec.md:305-306) and the card (spec.md:434-436) show 'Ever Teams — last used 5 minutes ago' and a 'Manage in Ever ID ↗' link. plan.md:193 stores only { clientId, lastSeenAt }. The settings (plan.md:414-424) and getPublicConfig (plan.md:366-372) hold no clientId→display-name map and no account-management URL, and EVER_ID_LIMITS (plan.md:250-277) has no 30-day constant. ACC-12-36 (T26, tasks.md:316-318) cannot assert an app name.
gaps.proposedFix: Add a settings key (for example delegatedClientNames: {clientId, displayName}[] ≤ 10) and accountManagementUrl (https) to the settings schema and getPublicConfig or the /identities response. Add delegatedClientsWindowDays: 30 to EVER_ID_LIMITS, and say where the filter runs.

gaps.title: The i18n key list misses strings the spec and tasks require
gaps.evidence: The plan §8 list (plan.md:646-691) has no keys for: the sign-out dialog title and buttons (spec.md:465-466); the S2 terms checkbox label (spec.md:418); the 'pending cookie expiry copy' that T25 tests (tasks.md:308); the admin §6.7 copy (Test connection, one row per check id, Health labels); the S22 'account disabled' message, which the spec calls existing but which is absent from en.json auth.error (keys: generic, invalidCredentials, emailNotVerified, accountLocked, sessionExpired, …); and web mappings for error codes everIdDisabled, sessionRequired, lastSignInMethod, notConnected and accountDisabled (plan.md:279-294, 610). T27 only checks the §8 list, so these would stay untranslated.
gaps.proposedFix: Add every missing key with its English value to plan §8. Give the ever_id_<snake_code> → key mapping for every EverIdErrorCode the web can receive, and extend T27's list.

gaps.title: Undecided identity-provider choices (D1–D9) leave device-flow audience and cross-audience tokens unspecified
gaps.evidence: idp-options.md:4 has Status Proposed, and D1–D9 (idp-options.md:166-176) are unanswered; spec.md:586-600 holds six [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] items. P1 code depends on them: the CLI device request sends 'resource/audience per idp-options.md' (plan.md:627-628), but idp-options defines no such parameter. D5 (multi-audience token vs token exchange) decides T37 and APW-11 P2 (cross-platform.md:143-145, 329-330). T34 needs the real provider.
gaps.proposedFix: The owner answers D1–D9 (T1). Afterwards, write the exact device-authorization request parameters for audience and scope into plan §7, and the D5 outcome into cross-platform §4.2.

gaps.title: 'Also sign out of Ever ID' depends on a dialog, an origin flag and a return route that do not exist
gaps.evidence: T26 (tasks.md:315) modifies 'the sign-out dialog that calls logout()', and plan.md:593 relies on 'when the profile says the session came from Ever ID'. No sign-out dialog exists: DashboardSidebar.tsx:127-133 and CommandPalette.tsx:190-193 call logout() directly. No profile or API field exposing the session origin is defined; plan §2.1 lists every behaviour change and has none. GET /logout-url returns a URL 'with a state' (plan.md:474), but nothing says where that state is stored, which web route receives the post-logout return and validates it, or which post_logout_redirect_uri is registered (idp-options.md:180-191 lists none). The dialog copy (spec.md:465-466) has no keys in plan §8.
gaps.proposedFix: Specify: the new dialog component and every caller that routes through it; the origin signal (for example GET /api/auth/ever-id/session-origin, or a field on the existing profile response); a state cookie name and TTL; the web return route and its validation; the registered post-logout URI in idp-options §6.1; and the dialog i18n keys.

gaps.title: S6 'You were signed out of Ever ID.' notice has no mechanism
gaps.evidence: S6 (spec.md:112-115) shows the notice on the next page load. The back-channel notice does a plain DELETE of session rows (plan.md:164-166, 541-543), so the web only sees a 401, the same as an expired session. No marker, error code or web handling is defined. Key auth.everId.signedOutByProvider exists (plan.md:659), but no task renders it and T30's back-channel assertions (tasks.md:354-355) never check it.
gaps.proposedFix: Define a signal. For example, when a notice ends sessions, write a short-lived verification row keyed by the session tokenHash, and have authenticate() return a distinct 401 code (everIdSignedOut) that the web maps to the notice. Alternatively, define the web logic that reads such a code. Add the assertion to ever-id-backchannel-logout.spec.ts.

gaps.title: Provider-unavailable state, health timestamps and the 60-second disable bound have no store that works across replicas
gaps.evidence: FR-14 (spec.md:216-217) and plan.md:445 and 728 say issuer drift marks the plugin unavailable 'until an admin re-tests'. GET /admin/health returns discoveryRefreshedAt, jwksRefreshedAt and lastLogoutNoticeAt (plan.md:479). FR-5 (spec.md:188-190) requires the disable to take effect within 60 s. No persistence is defined: plugin availability today is per-process registry state (packages/agent/src/facades/oauth.facade.ts:92, 195 check p.state === 'loaded'). gaps.title: Cal.diy reports version 6.2.0, its newest tag is the old-licence v6.2.0, and GHCR has no image for it
gaps.evidence:
The version string cannot tell the MIT edition from the old-licence release:
- apps/web/app/api/version/route.ts returns `packageJson.version`, and apps/web/package.json at the pin has `"version": "6.2.0"`. So /api/version answers 6.2.0, the same string as the old-licence release.
- `gh api repos/calcom/cal.diy/tags`: the newest tag is v6.2.0 (commit 1c193cca8682b33b9866c792186033f7ef886682). There is no tag for the MIT edition.
- LICENSE at v6.2.0 is the mixed licence ('Portions of this software are licensed as follows'): https://github.com/calcom/cal.diy/blob/v6.2.0/LICENSE.
- `gh api /orgs/calcom/packages?package_type=container` lists only `cal.com-deps`: no GHCR image of the MIT edition. The Docker Hub listing named in the upstream README was not checked.
The Blueprint uses the version smoke as a health check only, but refresh procedure step 3 and the catalog ref range do not say to avoid tag/release resolution.

2) 'Refreshing the pin' step 3: 'pin a commit on main only; never resolve "latest tag" or "latest release"'.

4) Keep `build.strategy: dockerfile` and state why.

gaps.title: 'Telemetry disabled' for Cal.diy covers only the app's own telemetry
gaps.evidence:
Three telemetry sources, only one covered:
- `CALCOM_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1` gates only the app's page-view collector (packages/lib/telemetry.ts L39-L50).
- At run time, start.sh runs `yarn start` = `turbo run start --filter=@calcom/web` (root package.json L66). Turborepo telemetry is on unless `TURBO_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1` (https://github.com/vercel/turborepo/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/telemetry.mdx).
- At build, `next build` honours `NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED` (next.js v16.2.3 packages/next/src/telemetry/storage.ts L64). The Cal.diy Dockerfile declares no ARG for it (ARG list L6-L19), so a build argument cannot reach it.
For contrast, Umami's Dockerfile sets NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 in both stages (L39, L56).
Spec FR-23 ('Telemetry is disabled'), the README 'Telemetry' row and the works.yml comment overstate what the Blueprint achieves.
gaps.proposedFix:
1) Add to cal-diy works.yml env: `- { name: TURBO_TELEMETRY_DISABLED, value: '1' }` and `- { name: NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED, value: '1' }`.
2) FR-23 and the README row become 'The application's telemetry and run-time tooling telemetry are disabled. Build-time framework telemetry cannot be configured through the upstream Dockerfile at the pin.'
3) plan §7.1: add a row with these sources.

gaps.title: Cal.diy build-time NEXT_PUBLIC values (app identity, support address, web push, signup) are fixed by the upstream Dockerfile

gaps.title: Cal.diy memory, boot time and image size are still estimates; what the pin shows about the process tree
gaps.evidence:
Estimates in the draft: works.yml L89 `resources: { cpu: 500m, memory: 1536Mi, memoryLimit: 3Gi } # TODO(verify)`; build 4 CPU / 12Gi / 60 min (L71); plan §7.1 'hosted runners … 4 vCPU / 16 GB'. What the pin shows:
- Boot is start.sh → `npx prisma migrate deploy` → `npx ts-node --transpile-only scripts/seed-app-store.ts` → `yarn start` → `turbo run start` → `next start`. That is several Node processes plus turbo in one container.
- The runner copies the whole monorepo install (`COPY --from=builder-two /calcom ./`, L83), not the Next standalone output, although BUILD_STANDALONE=true, so the image is large.
- The build heap is 6144 MB (L13).
- Upstream's own container test waits 120 s, then polls /auth/login for up to 60 s (docker-build-and-test/action.yml L136-L150).
No measurement exists.
gaps.proposedFix:
1) Keep the TODOs.
2) README 'Unverified' item 4: 'measure on the verification lane: peak pod memory during boot (migrate + seed + start) and during one booking; boot-to-ready time; image size; build peak memory, disk and duration'.
3) plan §7.1 resources row: add 'the runner stage copies the full install (image size and build disk unmeasured)'.
4) ACC-13-07 evidence records these numbers.

gaps.title: Cal.diy signup CAN be closed at run time through the app's `disable-signup` flag; the build-time-only premise is wrong
gaps.evidence:
Three places say signup can only be closed at build time: works.yml L154-L156 TODO, README 'Unverified' item 6, and spec §9 [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: signup]. The pin shows a run-time mechanism:
- apps/web/app/api/auth/signup/route.ts L18-L36: `ensureSignupIsEnabled` refuses with 403 'Signup is disabled' when `NEXT_PUBLIC_DISABLE_SIGNUP === "true"` OR `featuresRepository.checkIfFeatureIsEnabledGlobally("disable-signup")`. Requests with an invite token are still accepted.
- apps/web/lib/signup/getServerSideProps.tsx L25-L70: the signup page redirects to an error page on the same flag.
- packages/prisma/migrations/20230601181657_disable_signup_feature_flag/migration.sql inserts row `disable-signup` (enabled false, type OPERATIONAL) into table "Feature".
- packages/prisma/schema.prisma `model Feature` (L1369): `slug` id, `enabled` Boolean default false, description, type, stale, lastUsedAt, createdAt.
- packages/features/flags/features.repository.ts L35-L50: an in-process cache of 5 minutes.
- An admin UI exists at apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/settings/(admin-layout)/admin/flags/page.tsx.
URLs: https://github.com/calcom/cal.diy/blob/6bc45298226f96ff79e0c070c8b2ce39727e8477/apps/web/app/api/auth/signup/route.ts and …/packages/prisma/migrations/20230601181657_disable_signup_feature_flag/migration.sql
gaps.proposedFix:
1) Replace the commented NEXT_PUBLIC_DISABLE_SIGNUP entry and its TODO in cal-diy works.yml with this job:
- name: close-signup
  when: first-deploy
  component: web
  timeoutSeconds: 300
  command: [sh, -c, "npx prisma db execute --schema /calcom/packages/prisma/schema.prisma --stdin <<'SQL'\nUPDATE \"Feature\" SET enabled = true WHERE slug = 'disable-signup';\nSQL\n"]
Confirm the CLI flags on the verification lane.
2) It runs once, so an administrator can reopen signup under Settings → Admin → Flags. Pods pick up the change within 5 minutes.
3) README 'Unverified' item 6 becomes 'Resolved: signup is closed at run time through the `disable-signup` feature flag (table "Feature"); invite links still work'. Add a matching facts-table row.
4) Spec §9 signup question: new premise 'closing signup needs no rebuild'. Default: closed by the first-deploy job. The owner only confirms the default.
5) plan §7.1: add a row for the decision.

gaps.title: Umami 'default credential refused' smoke is already expressible; smoke calls take a request body
gaps.evidence: Five places treat a smoke request body as unavailable: umami works.yml L126-L127 (TODO(verify, APW-06) with the entry commented out), README 'Unverified' item 5, spec §9 [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: request bodies in smoke tests], plan §6 closing paragraph ('CONTRACTS §1 smoke has no body'), and tasks T43. gaps.title: Cal.diy sign-in page calls the auth base URL server-side; readiness and the pre-publish login smoke depend on it
gaps.evidence:
How the call is made:
- apps/web/server/lib/auth/login/getServerSideProps.tsx: once a user exists, it returns `csrfToken: await getCsrfToken(context)`.
- next-auth 4.24.13 (apps/web/package.json) resolves that server-side against `NEXTAUTH_URL_INTERNAL ?? NEXTAUTH_URL` (packages/next-auth/src/react/index.tsx L52-L59, L182: https://github.com/nextauthjs/next-auth/blob/next-auth@4.24.13/packages/next-auth/src/react/index.tsx).
- It logs CLIENT_FETCH_ERROR and returns null on failure (client/_utils.ts L52-L58).
- The Blueprint sets NEXTAUTH_URL to the PUBLIC URL.
Why it matters:
- APW-06 plan §5.5 order is first-deploy jobs → in-cluster smoke → publish Ingress. So the `login` smoke and every readiness probe after bootstrap make a server-side request to an address that is not yet published. Probe timeout defaults to 5 s (APW-03 schema §10).
- Upstream README L602-L604 (CLIENT_FETCH_ERROR troubleshooting) describes the same loop-back need.
- `next start` listens on 0.0.0.0 by default (next.js v16.2.3 cli).
- The works.yml comment on `needsHairpin: true` gives a generic reason.
Observed at pin: the redirect before the first user is 307 (upstream's own container test accepts 200 or 307, docker-build-and-test/action.yml L143-L145).
gaps.proposedFix:
1) Add to cal-diy works.yml env: `- { name: NEXTAUTH_URL_INTERNAL, value: 'http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/auth' }` with the comment 'server-side auth calls stay inside the pod (next-auth reads NEXTAUTH_URL_INTERNAL first)'.
2) Change the `needsHairpin` comment to name what still needs it: absolute links and redirects built from NEXT_PUBLIC_WEBAPP_URL.
3) README facts table: add the row '/auth/login server props call the auth base URL server-side (next-auth 4.24.13)'.
4) README 'Unverified' list: add 'login smoke answers 200 before the ingress is published'.

gaps.title: FR-21 (build placeholders, real secrets only at run time) contradicts the upstream README's 'Must match build variable'
gaps.evidence:
The contradiction: upstream README L574-L575 says NEXTAUTH_SECRET and CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY 'Must match build variable': https://github.com/calcom/cal.diy/blob/6bc45298226f96ff79e0c070c8b2ce39727e8477/README.md#L574-L575. Reading the source supports FR-21 instead:
- next.config.ts L50-L51 only checks presence and has no `env` block that inlines them.
- Every apps/web usage (code search: auth/setup, oauth token routes, two-factor totp routes, login server props) is server code that reads process.env at run time.
- packages/lib/crypto.ts uses the key as a latin1 AES-256 key, so 32 characters is required.
- Upstream's own docker-build-and-test action builds WITHOUT these args (Dockerfile defaults `secret`, L11-L12) and runs the image with different values, checking only /auth/login (action.yml L112-L158).
No sign-in or encrypted-credential round trip with different values has been observed. README and plan §7.1 cite only the Dockerfile.
gaps.proposedFix:
1) README 'Unverified' list: add 'Run-time NEXTAUTH_SECRET / CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY that differ from the build placeholders: sign-in and one encrypted round trip (two-factor setup) work. The upstream README says they must match; the source at the pin reads them only at run time.'
2) README facts table and plan §7.1 'No real secret as a build argument' row: add 'next.config.ts has no env inlining; all usages are server routes'.
3) T46: add the round-trip assertion.

gaps.title: No machine-readable API contracts for about 100 new operations, although MCP tool schemas are generated from OpenAPI
gaps.evidence: CONTRACTS §4 lists about 75 method/route entries (64 distinct paths). APW-10 plan §6.1 adds about 21 operator routes, and APW-12 adds the /api/auth/ever-id/* family. All are described only in prose tables (e.g. APW-07 plan §5, APW-09 plan §5, APW-10 plan §6). The real contract is generated code-first: apps/api/src/openapi/generate-openapi.ts builds it from Nest decorators, and apps/mcp builds tool input schemas from that document (OpenApiLoaderService; ToolRegistrationService.buildToolParameters(requestBody)). A missing @ApiProperty therefore silently removes a tool parameter. Tasks only check 'routes appear in the generated OpenAPI document' (APW-03 tasks.md:245/420/590, APW-04 tasks.md:326); there is nothing to compare request/response shapes, status codes or security against. Response envelopes already differ between epics (APW-09 `{ data, meta }`, APW-07 `{ entries, summary }`), and APW-07 uses DELETE with a JSON body (`{ confirmSlug }`), whereas the house pattern for deletes is POST /api/works/:id/delete. Upstream Spec Kit puts API definitions under contracts/.

gaps.title: Error code naming is inconsistent across epics and departs from the API's snake_case convention
gaps.evidence:
Three styles are in use:
- snake_case: APW-01 plan.md:452 `app_works_disabled`, `app_runtime_unavailable`; APW-02 plan.md:495-507 `not_found`, `sync_in_progress`, `retry_limit_reached`.
- camelCase: APW-04 plan.md:629 `provisioningUnavailable`; APW-05 plan.md:874 `notAppWork`, `buildNotFound`, `rebuildRateLimited`; APW-07 plan.md:652 `secureStorageUnavailable`, `confirmationMismatch`; APW-09 plan §5 `activeProposal`, `rateLimited`; APW-12 plan.md:493-505 `everIdDisabled`, `transactionInvalid`, although its redirect uses `ever_id_<snake_code>`.
- SCREAMING_SNAKE: APW-10 plan §6 `APPS_TIER_OPEN_REFUSED`, `QUOTA_CEILING_EXCEEDED`.
The same situation (a Work that is not kind app) is `404 not_found` in APW-02 but `404 notAppWork` in APW-05/07. On develop, apps/api/src has 55 snake_case `code: '…'` literals and no camelCase ones (e.g. `gh_repo_access_denied`, `backup_not_found`), under the `{ status: 'error', code, message }` envelope. The web translates these codes into i18n keys, and Constitution X makes codes public contract.
gaps.proposedFix: Add a 'Error codes' section to CONTRACTS.md, or a new contracts/errors.md referenced from SK-07's fragments. Rules: snake_case, append-only, body `{ status: 'error', code, message, details? }`, one code per situation shared across epics (e.g. `not_app_work` for 404 on non-app Works), and a separate web i18n key per code (camelCase leaf). Catalog columns: code, HTTP status, owner epic, routes, details keys, i18n key. Align APW-04/05/07/09/10/12 plans and tasks, and APW-05's copy-parity test, to the catalog.

gaps.title: The program never decides which App Works routes agents may call through MCP, chat or the CLI
gaps.evidence: The only MCP whitelist change in the program is APW-01's `inspect_app_source` (plan §4.5). APW-02…12 plans contain no decision about apps/mcp or apps/cli. The existing whitelist already exposes deploy_work → POST /api/deploy/works/{id} (whitelist.ts:99), which APW-06 extends with a kind-app branch (CONTRACTS §4). App deploys, including managed-tier compute spend (README rule 12), would therefore become agent-callable without anyone deciding it. House practice is an explicit whitelist plus a spec per surface (apps/mcp/test/whitelist-missions-ideas.spec.ts, whitelist-tasks-inbox-goals-fleet.spec.ts), with human gates kept out (whitelist.ts:300-305 approve routes, omitArgs ['force'] / ['requireAllApprovers']). Undecided routes include: app-env PUT (secret values, dotenv import, replaceGenerated, acknowledgeNeverRotate), app-dependencies DELETE, app-license attest (a legal attestation), upstream-pull-requests propose/signed/withdraw, provision, builds, upstream sync, evolve, app-lifecycle remove, and /api/me/apps. R-6 says the CLI is refused identically, but no CLI command for App Works is planned.
gaps.proposedFix: Add docs/specs/features/app-works/contracts/agent-surfaces.md. For every CONTRACTS §4 route it records: MCP tool name or 'not exposed' with the reason (human gate, secret input, legal attestation), readOnlyHint/destructiveHint, omitArgs, chat tool, and CLI command or 'none in Wave n'. Rules: attest, signed, approvals, env writes and data-deleting flags are never MCP-exposed; deploy_work gets an explicit decision for kind app. Add one task per exposing epic to modify apps/mcp/src/openapi-tools/whitelist.ts and extend apps/mcp/test/whitelist-app-works.spec.ts (created by APW-01), and reflect the result in SK-07's x-mcp fields.

gaps.title: Nothing ties the dispatcher cron override to an env name, and the facade clone coalescing key omits expectExisting
gaps.evidence: T34: 'the five-field validation and fallback copied from data-repo-sync-dispatcher.task.ts' and 'invalid override falls back to the default cron'.
